requirements.text: is not a Mission grant binding: it does not make the joined OAuth grant Mission-bound

observation.normative: a Mission-joining PDP's decision-time join of an ordinary credential to a Mission (the Mission Authority Server's Mission Join, {{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server}}) creates no grant binding: the joined OAuth grant remains unbound, the join's outcome is not persisted as this section's binding, and the same credential may join a different Mission on a later request without rebinding anything ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server}}, Section "Mission Join")

requirements.text: Non-active state gates every future derivation across every Mission grant binding ({{issuance-gating}}). It does not itself revoke an OAuth grant the same client or subject holds outside any Mission binding, and it does not recall an access token already issued before its `exp` absent a runtime state check the token's consumer performs ({{revocation}}, {{introspection}}).

observation.normative: terminating a Mission with two or more bound grant lineages refuses further derivation, at the token endpoint and on refresh, across every one of those lineages; it does not revoke an unrelated OAuth grant the same client or subject holds outside any Mission binding, and an access token already issued under the Mission remains valid per the stateless baseline until its own `exp`, or until a consumer performing a runtime state check ({{introspection}}) observes the non-active state

requirements.text: An AS that answers such a request through consent reuse, such as with a grant an authentication session holds for the client, MUST NOT select a grant bound to a Mission

observation.normative: an authorization request carrying no mission_intent, whose reusable candidate grant (the session's grant for the client, or a finished interaction's consent grant) is bound to a Mission, is never answered under that grant: no authorization code results under it, no derivation is counted against its Mission, and the grant, its binding and the session's reference to it stay intact. A grant is bound whatever record makes it so (a Mission's own grant, a delegation family, terminal or not, or a bound-grant index entry whose Mission no longer resolves). The rule excludes only bound grants: an independently ordinary grant still answers, its code carrying no Mission binding, and derivations against the existing binding (refresh, Token Exchange) still resolve to and count against its Mission
observation.local: oidc-provider's loadExistingGrant is loadReusableGrant (adapters/interaction-policy.ts): the provider default's candidate is classified by kernel.findByGrant, the delegation-family store's wasEverFamily and the bound-grant index, and a request carrying mission_intent keeps the default selection. With no eligible grant the reference AS refuses access_denied interactively (its only interaction is the Mission approval, whose render and decision finish an ordinary request's interaction refused) and consent_required under prompt=none (oidc-provider's consent checks); its descriptions name no Mission. Neither code is a protocol requirement: an AS may serve ordinary consent instead

requirements.notes: #1259 (D476). Before the fix, an ordinary request in a user agent holding an approved Mission's session grant received a code under that grant, and its redemption carried the earlier Mission's mission_id and spent one of its derivations. Mutation proofs: removing the exclusion fails all eight witnesses (the bound-grant witnesses receive codes, and the unresolvable index entry instead refuses at code mint with a description naming the Mission); classifying by findByGrant alone fails the family and unresolvable-index witnesses; reading the family by live resolution fails the terminal-family witness; dropping findByGrant fails the index-gap witness; leaving the consent-result candidate unclassified fails its witness; excluding every grant fails the ordinary-grant witness; destroying the excluded grant fails the intact-grant assertions and the refresh. The family, index-gap, unresolvable-index and consent-result candidates are store-seeded: no reference flow produces them for an ordinary request. The local outcome (access_denied with no server error from the approval surface's render or decision, and login_required keeping its precedence under prompt=none) has its own witnesses in the same describe block, outside this row.

requirements.text: A credential the Mission Issuer derives MUST have an `exp` that does not exceed the Mission's `expires_at`

observation.normative: no derived credential's exp exceeds the Mission's expires_at
observation.local: every credential the issuer derives under a Mission, driven per path against a Mission (or Child, successor or dispatched instance) ending inside the credential's configured lifetime: the code exchange's access token, refresh token, authorization code and ID Token; non-rotating and rotating refresh (access token and rotated refresh token); the async-delegation initial access token, family refresh token (which lives exactly until expires_at, with no 1 s floor, and is refused at the fractional-second boundary on both the exchange and the family refresh), family refresh access token and rotated family refresh token; the AROP deferred access token; the child-bound assertion and child access token; the dispatched instance access token; the expansion successor access token; the ID-JAG continuation grant; and the transaction token. A Mission past expires_at, or with under one second left, is refused rather than minted: invalid_grant mission_expired at the token endpoint (invalid_request, still with mission_error, on a Token Exchange; #1154), and access_denied at the authorization endpoint's resume, where the authorization code is minted. Not driven here, because this AS does not derive them from its own Mission: the cross-org audience-local token (bounded by the presented chain's leaf exp, whose nesting the chain verifier enforces; the cross-org companion governs that transitive bound), attenuation roots (clamped to expires_at in kernel/attenuation.ts but not reachable from an AS endpoint) and holder-signed attenuation children

observation.local: the cited test proves, for a refresh token issued to ap-agent (private_key_jwt): a refresh carrying only client_id, with no client authentication, is refused 401 invalid_client; a refresh authenticated as governed-agent with a DPoP proof for the same key is refused 400 invalid_grant, so the refusal comes from the client binding rather than a key mismatch; and the issuing client's authenticated refresh of the same token then succeeds. It exercises the async-delegation family refresh lineage only (a token also bound to the DPoP key); the code-flow refresh lineage, bound by client authentication alone, is not exercised. No mutation proof exists, because the authentication and client-mismatch checks are the provider library's (oidc-provider 9.10.0), outside src/

requirements.notes: #1503 finding 8 (D620): the AS issuance gate, split from the deployment routing row (core.rs-enforcement.delegated-routing-mission-aware), which keeps what the AS cannot verify. The condition is literal: any Mission-bound token carrying an emitted act chain, so the cross-org exchange and transaction tokens are witnessed alongside same-Mission delegation (#869). Refusal: the delegated exchange refuses a target that enforces the Mission's authorization_details (the shipped payments audience with its constraints keys) but is classified mission_aware false, with the gate's own reason, no token, and no derivation counted; that target's Resource Server does process act, so the refusal follows the AS's established classification, not the target's token handling. Issuance: the same target classified mission_aware true receives the delegated token. Mutation: disabling the exchange's own check alone leaves the save-time customizer backstop refusing invalid_target with the same reason, but after the derivation is counted, so the first witness fails on its count (expected 3 to be 2); refusing every audience at that check fails the issuance witnesses (18 tests, 400 instead of 200); making delegatedRoutingRefusal ignore the classification fails every refusal witness cited here (200 instead of 400). The customizer backstop's own branch is witnessed by the third and eighth tests.

requirements.notes: #825 acceptance item 7 (D402): introspection and the resource read the Mission access-token profile with one reader, readMissionAccessProfile in @mission/core (the typed claim set and its clock bounds, the `mission` claim's members, the authority through parseCredentialAuthority, a present `act` through the Actor Profile's validateActChain (#904, D428), and `cnf` structure through parseConfirmation), and run one negative-vector list, @mission/core/test-vectors. Each adds only its own rule: the resource requires the DPoP key it proves possession of; introspection requires `cnf` where the token's profile requires sender constraint and never proves possession, as Composite Active State says. The authority read only gates; the projection still reads the raw entries, delegation and capability bindings included. Sender constraint is required where a draft requires it of the issued token: a delegated token (the OAuth binding's Delegation section), a Child Mission's token (child-delegation, Attenuation Rules) and a dispatched template instance's token (the Template's Dispatch request and response, and its Dispatch Handoff), identified by the record's template basis. The Child Mission case stubs the kernel read; the dispatch case re-signs a real dispatched token. #250: a delegated token minted before a restart, whose issuance record the restart lost, is correctly signed under the key ring and introspects bare inactive while its Mission is active, where it introspected active before the restart. Proven by disabling the code it covers: reading a missing issuance record as the Mission's approval grant answers it active. #831 A2: an at+jwt this AS signed under another role's key is unresolvable and answers {active: false}; reverting introspection to every role's key makes it active.

observation.local: The reference resolves a credential's grant from its issuance record. A backing grant past its own lifetime fails the same Grant.find check as a revoked one, but no test drives grant expiry: every reference grant outlives the designations derived under it.

requirements.notes: #1503 finding 11 (D620). Each witness is proven by its own mutant. isGrantLive ignoring the backing grant, or the handle mint recording none, fails the self-exchange witness (200 instead of 400). The delegated exchange settling under a fresh Mission-bound grant instead of the designation's fails the depth-2 witness (200 instead of 400). Skipping the redemption's grant check fails all five cited tests. With the status and error assertions removed, the zero-count assertion alone fails under each mutant (the self-exchange witness counts 2 more, the depth-2 witness 1 more). On owner review of #1601 at 6f106618 (P2): isGrantLive stopped after eight backing hops while the issuer kept minting handles, so the ninth consecutive self-exchange minted a handle no designation could use. requirements.notes: D-2 of the OAuth binding layering plan; #1567. Two witnesses, each proved by its own mutation. A credential narrower than its Mission: narrowing the redemption from the Mission's full Authority Set instead fails it (the delegated token regains payments:invoice.list). A designation narrower than its credential: the deferring deployment's policy, deciding per entry, denies payments:vendor.read at designation and permits it at redemption. Recording the delegating credential's authority at designation and narrowing the redemption from it instead of the designation's claims (a mutation) fails only that witness, the delegated token gaining payments:vendor.read; the file's other 51 tests pass. Its control designation, issued after the change, carries and delivers both entries. In the reference AS a designation carries the presented authority within the Mission's current effective authority, narrowed by delegate eligibility, and the redemption re-applies both, so the two authorities differ only when eligibility or the effective authority widens between designation and redemption. The second witness constructs the eligibility case.

requirements.notes: #1535 finding 9 (D649, -01). Mutation: answering a failed commit with 200 fails the cited test (expected 200 to be 503). Partial (#1638 review; #1659, D771): the failure path is the first cited test. The ordering witness, on a file-backed store, reads at response release (where send() retains the bytes it delivers), not at signing, through a second connection rather than the writing one: the writing connection holds no open transaction, and the second connection already sees the transition, its version and the claimed nonce. Mutation: releasing the acknowledgement inside the transition's transaction fails it on the open transaction, and, with that assertion removed, on the second connection's read (state active, version 1). Configuration (#1684, D826): every file-backed kernel writer connection runs WAL with synchronous=FULL, set and read back on its first open and after reopening (a reopened WAL file otherwise runs at WAL's default, NORMAL), under normal locking, or exclusive under a recovery witness. FULL adds a WAL synchronization at each commit, which supports power-loss durability where the storage stack honors synchronization; no test here proves that. Crash/restart witnesses (#1684): the AS runs in a child process on a file-backed store, is killed with SIGKILL at a deterministic barrier, and is reopened on the same files with the WAL preserved. After an acknowledged revocation, the terminal state, its version and the retained response survive, and the retransmit replays the same bytes with no second transition; killed between the commit and the response's retention, the retransmit is finalized from the retained observation with its original iat, exp and fresh_until, never executed again. Mutations: dropping the response's retention fails both witnesses; dropping FULL fails both on the reopened writer connection; re-dating the finalized observation, or executing the committed row again, fails the commit-to-retention witness. Tested after the owner's review (#1707 at 8ee2069e): process-crash evidence plus asserted durability configuration; survival of an operating-system crash or power loss rests on synchronous=FULL and the storage stack, which no test proves.

requirements.text: The AS MUST process a lifecycle request in this order, refusing it at the first step that fails:

observation.normative: for discharge, the request syntax, its own members included, precedes the authorization its companion defines, and that whole authorization (the distinct grant, then selector existence, condition membership and the discharge authority mapping) precedes deduplication: a malformed member is refused invalid_request to a caller without the grant or outside the target's mapping, alike for an unknown Mission; a caller without the grant, or outside the mapping, gets the not-found response, never a replayed discharge response or a divergent-retry invalid_request; and that refusal retains nothing
observation.local: parseDischargeMembers validates the members; kernel.authorizeDischarge decides the not-found collapse read-only (no expiry or schedule commit, no latch, no event record, no purge) against the target the shared dischargeRoute names (a recorded occurrence's target, a forwarded discharge's replacement, otherwise the named target), and kernel.discharge repeats it in its transaction. A refused discharge on an expired Mission therefore no longer commits the expiry it observes; the next expiry-materializing path does. The observed_at clock-bounds check depends on elapsed time, not on the request alone: parseDischargeMembers checks only its RFC 3339 syntax, and handleDischarge checks the bounds after deduplication, for a request processed fresh, so an authorized retransmit replays however far its observed_at has aged (#1544 re-review).

No fixture pins a different mapping on a carryover replacement than on its old child, so the route's forwarded and recorded targets are not distinguished by a test; one route decides them for both checks. D175 narrowly superseded (#1544 review ruling): pre-deduplication refusals are read-only; post-authorization processing keeps D175's hoisted expiry. A refusal decided during syntax validation or target authorization commits no expiry, schedule, discharge event, latch or nonce response; the effective expiry still governs authorization and issuance at once, and its persistence and publication wait for the next expiry-materializing path. Proved post-authorization by removing the hoisted materialization (the fingerprint-conflict test fails: the conflict's rollback undoes the expiry). #1544 re-review P2: proved by checking the observed_at window before deduplication (the aged-retry test gets 400 instead of the replayed 200) and by removing the window check (that test fails on its fresh-nonce request, and so does the malformed-request test on its skewed observed_at).

tests.name: the discharge operation on the lifecycle endpoint > commits atomically under a concurrency race: one discharged, one already_discharged, one increment

requirements.notes: PARTIAL (review of PR #622; note corrected for PR #658; linkage corrected per #641): the latch rows, version increment, and event-dedup row share one SQLite transaction (latchDischarge's accompany hook, kernel.ts:1563-1605), and the durable propagation enqueue (the onLifecycleCommit hook Signals turns into a signal_outbox job) fires only once that transaction commits and before any other kernel work runs, so no subscriber observes an enqueue without the latch; the concurrency test (two concurrent HTTP discharges, distinct nonces and event_ids: one discharged, one already_discharged, one increment) proves that funnel's serialization. Signals delivery is durable, not best-effort: PR #658 journals one signal_outbox job per (event, consumer) synchronously inside onCommit, claims each job under a claimed_until lease, redelivers the byte-identical SET under bounded backoff, and marks a job done only after every sink acknowledges (rows signals.delivery.persist-until-acknowledged, signals.delivery.same-event-redelivery, and signals.delivery.bounded-retry, all tested). What remains untested for THIS row is restart and crash durability of the in-memory kernel store: the reference deployment runs one process and one in-memory database per service (src/docs/control-plane-deployment.md:3), and no test interrupts the process between the transaction's commit and the propagation enqueue, or exercises recovery after a restart. PR #806 then generalized that propagation: durable event rows with per-subscriber delivery rows, drains serialized per outbox instance from boot and the request path, every disposition write guarded on the pending state and the originating attempt so a terminal disposition is monotone, and a file-backed single-writer store selectable through KernelOptions. That gap is a separate, deferred guarantee: multi-process claiming across two Authorization Server processes sharing a kernel store, tracked by #641 and triggered only once such a deployment is planned. It is not a precondition for this row's single-transaction atomicity, and the two-instance recovery test belongs to #641's future multi-process work, not to this row's coverage. A witness for this row's own gap now has the plumbing it needs, so what is missing is the witness itself: no test interrupts the process between this transaction's commit and the propagation enqueue, and none recovers a discharge after a restart, which is why this row stays partial rather than tested. The remaining #641 work is a different guarantee, not this row's prerequisite: this row asserts single-transaction atomicity across the latch, version increment, and propagation enqueue, while #641 asserts multi-process claiming over that store once it exists.

requirements.notes: For a carried old child, kernel.discharge checks the targeted entry's own latch before resolving any pairing (applyDischarge with latchFirst, so the old child's terminal state does not turn it into terminal_noop). A byte-identical retransmission replays the stored bytes; a fresh-nonce replay (in the other target form) returns a new receipt echoing the new nonce, with no second commit.

requirements.text: The AS MUST resolve and validate the `discharge_authority` value whenever a condition first enters an immutable Mission-record entry

observation.normative: discharge_authority is resolved and validated whenever a condition enters an immutable Mission-record entry, including a condition a derived entry adds after activation (child creation, expansion, or another derivation), refusing the Intent or derivation when the selector maps to nothing

tests.name: terminal_when: derivation, subset rule, and selector resolution > fails closed when a discharge_authority value maps to nothing, at approval and at child creation

requirements.notes: IMPLEMENTED and tested: `assertDischargePoliciesResolvable` runs in the derivation (`MissionKernel.derive`) and in `insertRecord`, the single Mission-record creation funnel (approve, expansion, template dispatch, child creation), and refuses when a selector maps to nothing; the policy fails closed, so an unconfigured deployment cannot admit a condition at all. The test covers initial approval, the absent-baseline case, and a condition a CHILD CREATION adds after activation. Coverage stays partial because the row's declared surface is `lifecycle-endpoint` while the observable is a derivation/creation refusal: no lifecycle-endpoint request can introduce a condition, so no mapping can match this row's level and surface. The binding of the resolved mapping's identifier and version to the exact condition_digest in issuer-held metadata is NOT implemented: the mapping is resolved live from the issuer-held policy at each discharge instead.

requirements.text: The AS MUST NOT dereference `evidence_ref` in baseline processing and MUST NOT treat either member as authorization input.

observation.normative: the AS never dereferences evidence_ref during baseline discharge processing and never treats evidence_ref or evidence_digest as input to an authorization decision

tests.name: the discharge operation on the lifecycle endpoint > never dereferences evidence_ref and never lets an evidence member decide authorization

requirements.notes: Baseline processing validates `evidence_ref` (URI syntax, 512-character bound) and `evidence_digest` (prefix) and then only records them in the event store's audit columns; no code path fetches either. NON-DEREFERENCE is proven by a spy over globalThis.fetch across the discharge exchange (the AS runs in-process, so its own outbound calls are visible): the only recorded request is the test's own lifecycle POST, and none names the evidence host. A spy rather than an unreachable host is what makes this falsifiable, since a fetch the handler never awaits would still be recorded while leaving the response a prompt 200. NON-AUTHORIZATION is proven separately: the same evidence members presented by a caller lacking the discharge grant are still refused. What is NOT covered: a dereference performed outside this process (there is none) and any non-baseline processing a deployment might add.

requirements.text: The AS validates selector existence (`mission_id`, `entry_digest`, and `condition_digest` all resolve, the entry carries `terminal_when`, and `event_type` matches the named condition), then condition membership (the named condition belongs to the named entry), then target authorization

requirements.notes: The funnel checks selector existence and condition membership (one lookup: the condition is resolved INSIDE the named entry), then event_type match, then target authorization, and only then distinguishes a terminal Mission. The test revokes a Mission and presents an unknown entry_digest: the answer is the not_found collapse, not terminal_noop, so the terminal state is never a selector-existence oracle; the same terminal Mission with resolving selectors then answers terminal_noop.

observation.local: The scheduler arms an in-process timer for each committed schedule; the expiry clock also applies a due schedule on any read of the record, so a read after the deadline reports the committed transition before the timer is delivered. A scheduled revocation also destroys the Mission's OAuth grant, as a direct revoke does; that effect is a durable delivery of the committed terminal event (which names the schedule it applied), owed whether a read, a request or the timer committed it, and retried after a failure (the suspension schedule effects tests).

observation.normative: an authorized suspend against a suspended Mission carrying a valid suspend_until and on_expiry pair that differs from the recorded schedule, or arming one where none is recorded, updates the recorded pair and its committing party, emits the metadata change, and reports the new values in the signed response
observation.local: The replacement is a metadata-only commit (state unchanged, version incremented) whose lifecycle event carries prior_state and state suspended with the new suspend_until and on_expiry. The deadline compares as an instant, so the same instant in another RFC 3339 spelling is the recorded pair.

tests.name: suspension schedule record (@spec status#lifecycle-authorization, status#idempotency, status#mission-status-response, #1002) > records each committed schedule's committing party, and an authorized replacement updates the pair and its committing party, emits the change and reports the new values

requirements.notes: #1002 (D416). Proved by accepting a differing pair without effect, by emitting the commit without the schedule members, and by omitting them from the response (the test fails each time).

requirements.text: A `suspend` that omits both members leaves the recorded schedule, if any, and its committing party unchanged: omission never clears a deadline.

observation.normative: a suspend omitting both suspend_until and on_expiry against a suspended Mission leaves the recorded pair and its committing party unchanged, whoever sends it, and the deadline still applies
observation.local: The recorded pair sent again by another authorized caller is not a replacement either: its committing party stays.

tests.name: suspension schedule record (@spec status#lifecycle-authorization, status#idempotency, status#mission-status-response, #1002) > leaves the recorded schedule and its committing party unchanged on a suspend omitting both members, whoever sends it, and on the recorded pair sent again; the deadline still applies

requirements.notes: #1002 (D416). Proved by clearing the schedule on a plain suspend and by treating the recorded pair as a replacement (the test fails each time).

requirements.text: A `suspend` carrying only one of the two remains invalid

observation.normative: a suspend carrying suspend_until without on_expiry, or on_expiry without suspend_until, is refused as malformed and changes neither state nor any recorded schedule

tests.name: Mission Lifecycle endpoint authorization and request members (@spec status#lifecycle-authorization, status#mission-lifecycle-endpoint, #1191) > refuses schedule members on another operation, as an incomplete pair, and as a schedule this deployment cannot honor, leaving the Mission unchanged

Mission Lifecycle endpoint authorization and request members (@spec status#lifecycle-authorization, status#mission-lifecycle-endpoint, #1191) > parses the schedule members only on suspend, and only as a complete pair

suspension schedule record (@spec status#lifecycle-authorization, status#idempotency, status#mission-status-response, #1002) > refuses either schedule member alone against a suspended Mission with a recorded schedule invalid_request, changing neither its state nor its schedule

requirements.notes: #1191 witnesses the refusal on an active Mission and the parse; #1002 adds a suspended Mission with a recorded schedule. Proved by reading an incomplete pair as no schedule (all three tests fail).

requirements.text: A retransmit that arrives while the original is still being processed never commits the operation a second time

observation.normative: a retransmit concurrent with its original commits no second transition, and every answer reports the one committed operation's outcome
observation.local: the nonce claim commits inside the transition's transaction; a retransmit that finds the claim still committed (the original still signing) finalizes it from the retained observation, never re-executing the operation, and every exchange delivers the response retained first, so the original, a concurrent retransmit and a later replay carry the same bytes

tests.name: a retransmit concurrent with its original commits once and answers with the one response (@spec status#idempotency, #1724 C1) > a resume retransmitted while the original is still being signed commits one transition, and the original, the retransmit and a later replay answer the same 200 response byte for byte

requirements.notes: #1724 C1 (D847). The witness holds the original `resume` at its signature, after its commit, and retransmits in that window. Proved by two defects: dropping the deduplication lookup (the retransmit re-executes and answers `conflict`), and delivering each exchange's own signature instead of the retained one (the original and the retransmit answer with different envelopes, which the reference did before this change).

requirements.text: the client MAY accept it as confirmation of its original operation's outcome when it correlates the response to that retained request (its `mission_id` and `nonce`) and every other check passes.

observation.normative: a client accepting an expired replay correlates it to its retained request and passes every other check, uses no compromised key, and treats it as confirmation of that outcome only: no cache refresh, no action authorized, no current state established
observation.local: the reference Lifecycle client (demo lifecycle-client.ts, verifyLifecycleResponse) verifies through the shared verifier's report-expiry mode, which classifies a response as expired when it is verified on or after its exp whatever the skew tolerance, with keys read afresh from the validated metadata's jwks_uri at each verification and limited to its trusted Status kids; an expired replay that correlates and passes every other check returns a confirmation carrying no Mission object

tests.name: the reference Lifecycle client's verification of an expired replay (@spec status#idempotency, status#mission-status-response) > accepts the AS's replay of its retained request, verified after its exp, only as confirmation of that request's outcome, which carries no Mission state

the reference Lifecycle client's verification of an expired replay (@spec status#idempotency, status#mission-status-response) > refuses an expired replay that does not correlate to the retained request: another request's nonce, or another Mission

the reference Lifecycle client's verification of an expired replay (@spec status#idempotency, status#mission-status-response) > refuses an expired replay that fails any other check: an audience or a sub naming another client, or a kid its configuration does not trust

the reference Lifecycle client's verification of an expired replay (@spec status#idempotency, status#mission-status-response) > takes a replay at or past its exp as confirmation only, inside the 30 second skew allowance and beyond it, and one second before its exp as an observation (#1757 review)

the reference Lifecycle client's verification of an expired replay (@spec status#idempotency, status#mission-status-response) > refuses the AS's replay of its retained request once the Status key that signed it is compromised, before and after its exp

the shared Mission Status verifier, reporting expiry on request (@spec status#mission-status-response, status#idempotency) > refuses a response whose exp has passed by default, and on request returns it marked expired once every other check passes

the shared Mission Status verifier, reporting expiry on request (@spec status#mission-status-response, status#idempotency) > classifies expiry by exp and the verification time alone: current one second before exp, expired at exp and after it, inside the tolerance and beyond it, at the profile's tolerance and at zero (#1757 review)

the shared Mission Status verifier, reporting expiry on request (@spec status#mission-status-response, status#idempotency) > still refuses an expired response that fails any other check: another audience, another issuer, another Mission, a fresh_until after exp, or a key it does not hold, at its exp, just after it and long after, at the profile's tolerance and at zero

requirements.notes: #1724 C1 (D847), normative client rule. Every observation clause witnessed: correlation (the non-correlating replays are refused), every other check (audience, sub, an untrusted kid; and in the shared verifier, issuer, Mission, fresh_until and key), no compromised key (the AS's replay of the original bytes under the Status key compromised after a restart on the same kernel store is refused), and confirmation only (no Mission object). Proved by eight defects: correlation skipped when expired; the expected Mission taken from the response; report mode accepting any claim failure; the client sub check dropped; published keys cached across verifications; every published key accepted; expiry reported by default; an expired replay returned as an observation. #1757 review: expiry is classified by the verified exp and the verification time, never the skew tolerance (a replay just past exp inside the tolerance had come back as an observation, and at zero tolerance the re-verification at exp refused a valid expired replay); boundary witnesses at exp - 1, exp, exp + 1, inside and beyond the tolerance, and at zero tolerance. Proved by two more defects: tolerance-based classification, and re-verification at exp.

requirements.text: publishes it as revoked in its historical key set

observation.normative: a key the AS signed Mission Status or Lifecycle responses under that is known or suspected compromised is published as revoked in the AS's historical key set, so the archived responses it signed stay verifiable and classifiable
observation.local: The AS lists its Status role's generations withdrawn as compromised in the historical key set it serves at mission_historical_jwks_uri (kernel/historical-key-set.ts).

tests.name: an AS across a Status key compromise (@spec status#historical-key-set, status#as-metadata, #831 B3) > publishes no set before the compromise; after it, advertises mission_historical_jwks_uri and serves the withdrawn key, revoked, signed under the replacement

requirements.notes: #1535 finding 8 (D649): the issuance profile's Signing and Key Rotation compromise rule, applied to the Status signing key. History: specified but not implemented (D405) until the ring's compromise operation (#831 B2 (#1681, D809)) and the historical key set (#831 B3 (#1766)). #831 B1 (D774): re-anchored to the retention section and re-quoted; the publication is the historical key set, not the jwks_uri. #831 B3: the endpoint witness compromises the Status key across AS boots and finds the withdrawn key listed, revoked. Proven by not listing withdrawn generations, which fails it. D931 per-row review: tested. Obligation: a key known or suspected compromised is published as revoked in the historical key set. Witness: the endpoint test compromises the Status key across AS boots and finds the withdrawn key listed under its original kid and material, revoked. Scope: under a key ring; per-boot Status keys (`MISSION_EPHEMERAL_KEYS=1`) are the documented development mode, which strands a prior boot's responses (`channel-key-matrix.md`, D913). Only the Status role signs Status and Lifecycle responses, and a compromise takes effect at the AS's next start (D806: stop, edit, start).

requirements.text: A consumer MUST NOT accept, for a current reliance decision, a response signed under a key the AS has published as compromised.

observation.normative: a consumer refuses to rely, for a current decision, on a Mission Status Response whose signing key the AS has published as compromised, although the archived response still verifies for audit under the key's historical public JWK
observation.local: The PDP's Status consumer (refreshingStatusKeys with the issuer's mission_historical_jwks_uri) refuses, for current reliance, a key its held historical key set lists, even while its cached jwks_uri still carries it, and keeps every key it has learned as compromised: no later set, replaying or replacing, removes one, a set a learned-compromised key signed is refused, and a failed refetch keeps them; with none ever verified, the jwks_uri rule alone decides. The Signals receiver's resynchronization (#1810) holds the Status keys as the PDP does (`missionStatusIssuer(...).keys`): a response under a key the set lists is refused, as its first verification (which fetches the set) and after one under the current key, and the held Mission stays held, though its configured kids and cached jwks_uri still carry the key; the same issuer advertising no set resynchronizes on it.

tests.name: a listed key and a current reliance decision (@spec status#signing-key-retention, status#historical-key-set, #831 B3) > never verifies a current response under a key the set lists, though a cached jwks_uri still carries it

what the consumer learns as compromised, it keeps (@spec status#historical-key-set, status#signing-key-retention, #831 B3, D887) > refuses a replacement set signed under a learned-compromised key, whether it empties the set or lists the current key

what the consumer learns as compromised, it keeps (@spec status#historical-key-set, status#signing-key-retention, #831 B3, D887) > keeps a learned revocation through a replayed older or empty set the current key signed

the historical key set through the configured issuer (@spec status#historical-key-set, status#mission-status, #831 B3, D901) > refuses, through missionStatusIssuer, a key the advertised set lists while the cached jwks_uri still carries it

the Signals receiver's Status keys (@spec status#signing-key-retention, status#historical-key-set, #1810) > refuses a resynchronization response signed under a key the issuer's historical key set lists, though its configured kids and its cached jwks_uri still carry it; the set is what refuses it

requirements.notes: #1535 finding 8 (D649). History: specified but not implemented (D405) until the ring's compromise operation withdrew the key from the jwks_uri (#831 B2 (#1681, D809)), the Status consumers refreshed it (#831 C (#1697, #1705, D833)), and they refused a key the historical key set lists (#831 B3 (#1766)). The Mandate profile's compromise-time classification stays an informative pointer and is not a Status consumer duty. #831 B1 (D774): re-anchored to the retention section. #831 B3: the witness shows the same response accepted by a consumer holding no set, so the set is what refuses it. Proven by dropping the refusal. D887 (owner review of #1766): a replacement or replayed set could erase a learned revocation; the holder keeps what it learned, witnessed by an empty replacement signed under the compromised key and a replayed empty set signed under the current key, and proven by replacing the learned set on refresh. D931 per-row review: stays partial. Witnessed for the PDP's Status consumer: a listed key is refused while a cached jwks_uri still carries it, through `refreshingStatusKeys` and through `missionStatusIssuer`, and learned compromise survives replacement and replayed sets and failed refetches. Gap: the reference's Lifecycle consumer (`demo/src/lifecycle-client.ts`, `verifyLifecycleResponse`) fetches the `jwks_uri` for every verification and keeps no cache, so it never relies on a cached copy and a failed fetch accepts nothing, but no cited test exercises it. D901: the consumer configured from issuer metadata (`missionStatusIssuer`, which the separated MAS pilot uses) takes the set's URI from the validated metadata and refuses a listed key its cached jwks_uri still carries; a present but malformed `mission_historical_jwks_uri` is refused rather than ignored. Mutation: dropping the URI from the helper fails that witness. #1810 (option A, on the owner's go): the Signals receiver's resynchronization took a pinned key set and never read the historical key set; it now takes the Status keys as a key resolver, held through `missionStatusIssuer`, and refuses a listed key. Witnessed with a control: the same issuer advertising no set resynchronizes on the key. Proven by restoring the pinned key set and by dropping the set's refusal; each fails the witness at the refusal. Stays partial for the Lifecycle consumer.

requirements.text: The AS MUST keep the public JWK for every `kid` it has signed such a response under resolvable for at least the Mission's audit horizon

observation.normative: every key the AS signed a Mission Status or Lifecycle response under stays resolvable for the Mission's audit horizon: a retired key in its jwks_uri, a compromised key in its historical key set
observation.local: A retired Status generation stays in the jwks_uri until its confirmed stop plus the longer of the audit horizon and the longest Mission lifetime (#831 B2); a compromised one stays resolvable in the historical key set (#831 B3).

tests.name: an AS across a Status key compromise (@spec status#historical-key-set, status#as-metadata, #831 B3) > publishes no set before the compromise; after it, advertises mission_historical_jwks_uri and serves the withdrawn key, revoked, signed under the replacement

rotating, retiring and compromising a role's generations (@spec #831 B2) > retirement waits for the retention deadline from the confirmed stop, refuses when none can be established, and refuses a Status generation a standing consent depends on

requirements.notes: History: specified at #831 B1 (D774). #831 B2 (#1681, D809) keeps an overlap generation in the jwks_uri until its confirmed stop plus the longer of the audit horizon and the longest Mission lifetime, and refuses retirement when that cannot be established; #831 B3 (#1766) retains a compromised key in the historical key set. #831 B2 and B3: the unit witness holds a retirement to the retention deadline; the endpoint witness finds a compromised Status key resolvable in the historical key set after its withdrawal. D931 per-row review: tested. Obligation: every kid that signed a Status or Lifecycle response stays resolvable for at least the Mission's audit horizon, a retired key in the jwks_uri and a compromised key in the historical key set. Witnesses: the unit test holds a retirement to its deadline (the confirmed stop plus the longer of the audit horizon and the longest Mission lifetime) and refuses one it cannot establish; the endpoint test finds a compromised Status key resolvable in the historical key set after its withdrawal. The set keeps every listed key; nothing removes one. Scope: under a key ring; per-boot Status keys (`MISSION_EPHEMERAL_KEYS=1`) are the documented development mode, which strands a prior boot's responses (`channel-key-matrix.md`, D913).

requirements.text: the AS stops signing with it and removes it from its `jwks_uri`

observation.normative: a key known or suspected compromised signs no further response and is absent from the AS's jwks_uri
observation.local: Compromising a generation withdraws it from the jwks_uri and stops signing under it, activating a replacement in the same write (#831 B2).

tests.name: an AS across a Status key compromise (@spec status#historical-key-set, status#as-metadata, #831 B3) > publishes no set before the compromise; after it, advertises mission_historical_jwks_uri and serves the withdrawn key, revoked, signed under the replacement
rotating, retiring and compromising a role's generations (@spec #831 B2) > compromising the active generation withdraws it at once and activates a fresh replacement in the same write

requirements.notes: #831 B1 (D774): implemented by #831 B2 (#1681, D809): compromising a generation stops signing with it and withdraws it from the jwks_uri, witnessed in signing-key-rotation.test.ts. #831 B2 and B3: the unit witness withdraws the generation at once; the endpoint witness finds it absent from /jwks and the AS signing under the replacement. D931 per-row review: tested. Obligation: a compromised key signs nothing further and is absent from the jwks_uri. Witnesses: the unit test withdraws the generation at once and activates a replacement in the same write; the endpoint test finds it absent from /jwks and the kernel signing under the replacement. Scope: under a key ring; per-boot Status keys (`MISSION_EPHEMERAL_KEYS=1`) are the documented development mode, which strands a prior boot's responses (`channel-key-matrix.md`, D913). The withdrawal takes effect at the AS's next start (D806: stop, edit, start).

requirements.text: A consumer MUST NOT use a key from the historical key set to verify a response for a current reliance decision.

observation.normative: a consumer never verifies a response for a current reliance decision under a key it found only in the historical key set, whatever the key's state
observation.local: The current-reliance keys never resolve a key from the historical key set; auditKeys alone reads one, to verify an archived response.

tests.name: a listed key and a current reliance decision (@spec status#signing-key-retention, status#historical-key-set, #831 B3) > never falls back to the set for a current reliance decision once the jwks_uri no longer carries a listed key; only audit verification reads it

requirements.notes: History: specified at #831 B1 (D774); implemented in the Status consumers by #831 C (#1697, #1705, D833) and #831 B3 (#1766). #831 B3: proven by a current-reliance resolver that reads listed keys from the set, which this witness refuses. D931 per-row review: tested. Obligation: no consumer verifies a response for current reliance under a key found only in the historical key set. Witness: the PDP's current-reliance keys never resolve a listed key once the jwks_uri drops it, and only `auditKeys` reads the set. The reference's other Status and Lifecycle consumers (the Lifecycle client, the Signals receiver) never read the set at all.

requirements.text: A consumer MUST NOT rely on a cached copy of the AS's `jwks_uri` beyond the freshness lifetime its response explicitly declares

observation.normative: a consumer relies on a cached jwks_uri only within the freshness lifetime its response explicitly declares, then re-fetches and replaces its cached key set with the fetched one, never adding to it, so a removed key stops verifying within that lifetime
observation.local: The PDP's Status consumer holds the jwks_uri through IssuerKeys (#831 C), which uses a fetched set only within its explicit freshness lifetime. The Signals receiver's resynchronization holds its Status keys the same way (#1810): a key withdrawn from the jwks_uri still verifies within the cached set's declared lifetime, without a fetch, and once it ends the set is fetched again and the key refused.

tests.name: the Status consumer's jwks_uri freshness (@spec status#signing-key-retention, #831 B3) > relies on a cached jwks_uri only within the freshness lifetime its response declares

the Signals receiver's Status keys (@spec status#signing-key-retention, status#historical-key-set, #1810) > follows a Status key rotation within the jwks_uri's declared freshness: a newly published trusted key resynchronizes before the cached set's lifetime ends, and a withdrawn one stops once it ends, when the set is fetched again

requirements.notes: History: specified at #831 B1 (D774); implemented in the Status consumers by #831 C (#1697, #1705, D833). #831 B3: witnessed at the Status consumer, not the library. Proven by a fixed ten-minute lifetime. D931 per-row review: tested. Obligation: a cached jwks_uri is relied on only within the freshness lifetime its response explicitly declares, then replaced, never added to. Witness: within the lifetime the cached copy serves without a fetch; at its end the set is refetched and the withdrawn key refused. The Lifecycle client keeps no cache. #1810: the Signals receiver's resynchronization holds the jwks_uri through `missionStatusIssuer` (`IssuerKeys`), witnessed by a withdrawn key that verifies within the declared lifetime and is refused once it ends; proven by using the cached set past its lifetime, which fails the witness at the refusal.

requirements.text: A response without valid explicit freshness information is stale when received

observation.normative: a jwks_uri response without valid explicit freshness information is stale when received and is revalidated before reuse; the consumer never assigns it a heuristic lifetime
observation.local: A jwks_uri response without explicit freshness is stale when received, so the Status consumer revalidates it at every verification.

tests.name: the Status consumer's jwks_uri freshness (@spec status#signing-key-retention, #831 B3) > gives a jwks_uri response without explicit freshness no lifetime: every verification revalidates

requirements.notes: History: specified in the #831 B1 review (D780); implemented in the Status consumers by #831 C (#1697, #1705, D833). #831 B3: witnessed at the Status consumer. Proven by a fixed ten-minute lifetime. D931 per-row review: tested. Obligation: a jwks_uri response without valid explicit freshness is stale when received and revalidated before reuse, never given a heuristic lifetime. Witness: every verification refetches such a response. The Lifecycle client reuses no response.

requirements.text: When the cached set is stale and revalidation fails, the consumer MUST NOT accept a Status or Lifecycle response for a current reliance decision until a fetch or revalidation succeeds.

observation.normative: when the cached jwks_uri set is stale and revalidation fails, the consumer refuses current reliance on a Status or Lifecycle response until a fetch or revalidation of the jwks_uri succeeds
observation.local: When the stale jwks_uri cannot be revalidated, the Status consumer refuses the response, with no stale fallback.

tests.name: the Status consumer's jwks_uri freshness (@spec status#signing-key-retention, #831 B3) > refuses a Status response when the stale jwks_uri cannot be revalidated, never falling back to the stale copy

requirements.notes: History: specified in the #831 B1 review (D780); implemented in the Status consumers by #831 C (#1697, #1705, D833). #831 B3: witnessed at the Status consumer. Proven by a stale-if-error fallback. D931 per-row review: stays partial. Witnessed for the PDP's Status consumer: a stale jwks_uri that cannot be revalidated refuses the Status response, with no stale fallback, until a revalidation succeeds. Gap: the sentence names Status or Lifecycle responses. The reference's Lifecycle consumer (`demo/src/lifecycle-client.ts`, `verifyLifecycleResponse`) fetches the `jwks_uri` for every verification and keeps no cache, so it never relies on a cached copy and a failed fetch accepts nothing, but no cited test exercises it.

requirements.text: The AS signs the set under its active Mission Status signing key

observation.normative: the historical key set is a jwk-set+jwt signed under the AS's active Mission Status signing key, the key it currently signs Mission Status responses under; never under a listed key, a retired key or another role's key, and after that key's own compromise under its replacement, never another published key
observation.local: signHistoricalKeySet signs once at boot under the active Status key, the replacement after a Status compromise, and refuses a signer whose kid or key material the set lists.

tests.name: an AS across a Status key compromise (@spec status#historical-key-set, status#as-metadata, #831 B3) > publishes no set before the compromise; after it, advertises mission_historical_jwks_uri and serves the withdrawn key, revoked, signed under the replacement
the historical key set's listing and signer (@spec status#historical-key-set, #831 B3) > signs nothing when no key is withdrawn, and never under a key the set lists, by kid or by key material

requirements.notes: History: specified at #831 B1 (D774); implemented by #831 B3 (#1766). D780: restricted to the authorized active Mission Status key; membership in the jwks_uri is not authorization. #831 B3: the endpoint witness verifies the served set under the replacement Status key alone; the unit witness refuses a listed signer by kid and by material. Proven by signing under the transaction-token role's key, by dropping the signer check, and by checking the kid alone. D931 per-row review: tested. Obligation: the set is signed under the active Mission Status key, never a listed key or another role's, and after that key's compromise under its replacement. Witnesses: the endpoint test verifies the served set under the replacement Status key alone, the key the kernel now signs Status responses under; the unit test refuses a listed signer by kid and by key material. Scope: under a key ring; per-boot Status keys (`MISSION_EPHEMERAL_KEYS=1`) are the documented development mode, which strands a prior boot's responses (`channel-key-matrix.md`, D913).

requirements.text: A consumer MUST NOT accept a historical key set whose signature does not verify under the key its trusted configuration authorizes.

observation.normative: a consumer refuses a historical key set signed under any key other than the Mission Status signing key its trusted configuration authorizes, including another role's key, a retired key, a key the set lists, and a replacement its configuration does not yet authorize
observation.local: verifyHistoricalKeySet accepts a set only with typ jwk-set+jwt, the expected iss, and a signature under the consumer's configured Status keys; a replacement Status key signs only once the configuration names it.

tests.name: a historical key set's signer, from the consumer's configuration (@spec status#historical-key-set, #831 B3) > accepts a set signed under the configured Status key, and refuses one signed under another role's published key or an unconfigured replacement until the configuration names it

what the consumer learns as compromised, it keeps (@spec status#historical-key-set, status#signing-key-retention, #831 B3, D887) > refuses a replacement set signed under a learned-compromised key, whether it empties the set or lists the current key

requirements.notes: History: specified in the #831 B1 review (D780); #831 C (#1697, #1705, D833) gave the Status consumers role-bound trusted kids, and #831 B3 (#1766) the historical key set they validate. #831 B3: proven by skipping the signature check and by skipping the typ check. D931 per-row review: tested. Obligation: a consumer accepts a set only under the Mission Status key its trusted configuration authorizes. Witnesses: the PDP's holder refuses a set under another role's published key, an unconfigured replacement (until configured), a wrong typ, and a learned-compromised key. It is the reference's only reader of the set.

the historical key set's listing and signer (@spec status#historical-key-set, #831 B3) > lists each withdrawn key under its kid, with revoked: reason compromised, revoked_at and, only when established, compromised_at, as NumericDates

requirements.notes: History: specified at #831 B1 (D774); implemented by #831 B3 (#1766). #831 B3: proven by dropping the member, by emitting compromised_at when none is established, and by leaving the times as ISO strings. D931 per-row review: tested. Obligation: each listed JWK carries revoked with reason compromised, revoked_at, and compromised_at only when established, as NumericDates. requirements.text: The AS serves the set with the media type `application/jwk-set+jwt` ({{OpenID.Federation}}, Section 15.6).

observation.normative: the AS serves its historical key set with the HTTP Content-Type application/jwk-set+jwt

tests.name: an AS across a Status key compromise (@spec status#historical-key-set, status#as-metadata, #831 B3) > publishes no set before the compromise; after it, advertises mission_historical_jwks_uri and serves the withdrawn key, revoked, signed under the replacement

requirements.notes: #1774 (D931). requirements.text: The AS MUST implement per-consumer rate limiting (returning `rate_limited`, {{mission-status-errors}})

observation.local: a fixed window per authenticated client across both Status routes, default 120 requests per 60 seconds (`missionStatusRateLimit`). On the advertised form POST it is counted between request syntax and authorization (Processing Order steps 2 and 3), so a malformed request keeps its invalid_request refusal and no Mission has been read; on the development GET, after authentication. An unauthenticated request is an authentication failure and is not counted. The windows are in-process, as the deployment is single-process; a refused request is not counted; the limit is decided before any Mission is read, so the refusal is the same whichever Mission the request names

requirements.notes: #562: implemented and tested is the DETECTION half only (the receiver flags the need). Not covered: the actual Mission Status refetch (no consumer in this repo calls it off this signal). See signals.discharge.producer-authority-changed-emit and signals.discharge.producer-gating-undeclared-stream for the producer-side rows this issue left todo (no discharge funnel or mission_capabilities_supported gate exists in src/). #572 (review of #562) fixed two defects and added markRematerialized(missionId, observedBaseline) so the latch this row's tests exercise is no longer permanent; also fixed contain()'s authority_changed to key on an actual EFFECTIVE-set narrowing rather than merely reaching the metadata-only commit path (see containment.test.ts and this file's builder-emission describe block). Coverage stays 'partial': the acknowledgement is still consumer-invoked bookkeeping over the detect-only latch, and the actual Mission Status refetch this row's normative text requires 'before further consequential reliance' remains unwired in this repo. #287 residual (discharge implementation): the producer side is now real, so this row gains an end-to-end mapping in which a KERNEL DISCHARGE commit (not only a contain commit) drives the receiver to latch rematerialization, which is the case the rule was written for. Coverage stays 'partial' for the unchanged reason: the receiver DETECTS the need and no consumer in this repo performs the Mission Status refetch the clause requires before further consequential reliance. With a file-backed receiver store (#250) the latch and its marker survive a restart, and an acknowledgement that covers the marker clears it durably. #1747 (D942, D950): the receiver withholds its lease while the latch is set. A Mission Status response re-establishes state but never clears the latch, since a state-only response carries no effective authority; the latch clears only on the consumer's acknowledgement (markRematerialized) after it refreshed its audience-scoped effective authority, so no lease is relied on before that. requirements.text: The Mission Issuer MUST NOT re-enable the stream while an attempt to deliver a verification or heartbeat event on it is unresolved, or until more than the longer of `mission_max_stale_seconds` and the stream's heartbeat interval, plus any clock tolerance it allows its consumers, has passed since the latest such attempt ended, whether or not that attempt was acknowledged

observation.normative: a paused stream receives no Stream Updated enabled event, verification event or held event while a verification delivery attempt on it is unresolved, nor at or before the instant the longer of mission_max_stale_seconds and the stream's heartbeat interval, plus the clock tolerance, after the latest such attempt ended, whether that attempt was acknowledged, failed after the receiver processed it (its acknowledgement lost), or was left unresolved by a process that stopped; this holds for Transmitter-initiated and requested verification events and across an emitter restart over a persistent store, and a second withholding during the pause does not bring that instant forward; a consumer applying the staleness rule as written, including one whose clock runs behind the issuer's by the tolerance, has ended its reliance on cached Mission state by that instant
observation.local: the emitter's maxStaleSeconds option is the issuer's advertised mission_max_stale_seconds, its heartbeatIntervalSeconds option the agreed heartbeat interval and its clockToleranceSeconds option the clock tolerance (0 when absent), all configured at the construction site; the window is the longer of the first two plus the tolerance, and without both of the first two a paused stream is never re-enabled automatically. Each verification hand-off is journaled before it begins and ends when the sink's hand-off settles, acknowledged or failed, which the emitter takes as the instant it can exclude the attempt's receipt; an attempt a stopped process left unresolved ends when the next emitter opens the store, which assumes one emitter process per store. requirements.notes: #1877 (D1017). The acceptance case: liveness attested every 10 seconds, a contain commit withheld 5 seconds after the last verification delivered on the undeclared stream; at exactly that verification plus 60 seconds the stream is still paused and a model of Signals' staleness rule (stale after more than mission_max_stale_seconds without a verification or heartbeat event, latched until state is re-established) still permits reliance; 1 millisecond later the model has ended reliance while the stream has received only the paused notice; the stream re-enables after that, and the first verification after it does not restore reliance. With a 90-second heartbeat interval and mission_max_stale_seconds 60, the stream stays paused past the last liveness plus 60 seconds and at exactly plus 90, while the model, still verified live, permits reliance; 1 millisecond later reliance has ended and only then does the stream re-enable. Proved by mutation: halving the window fails six stream-pause tests; re-enabling at the bound rather than after it fails the acceptance, re-enable, restart and heartbeat-interval tests; a window of mission_max_stale_seconds alone fails the heartbeat-interval test; keeping the stream status in a TEMP table (not persisted) fails the restart test; keeping the first window on a second withholding fails the second-withholding test. #1877 review (D1023): the owner's probe, a verification acknowledged at 10 s and another received at 20 s with its acknowledgement lost, a narrowing withheld at 21 s, now keeps the stream paused at 70 s and re-enables only after 80 s; a requested verification whose acknowledgement is lost does the same; a hand-off still in flight past the window keeps the stream paused, and the window runs from when it ends; an attempt left unresolved by a stopped process ends at the reopening instant; a 5-second clock tolerance moves the re-enable instant 5 seconds later, past the point a consumer whose clock runs 5 seconds behind ends its reliance. Proved by mutation: recording the end of an attempt only when it is acknowledged fails four tests (the probe, the requested lost acknowledgement, the in-flight and the restart tests); re-enabling while an attempt is unresolved fails the in-flight test; dropping unresolved attempts on reopening instead of ending them fails the restart test; dropping the tolerance from the window fails the tolerance test.

requirements.notes: #1877 review (D1023). The owner's probe: a suspension committed, its delivery to the undeclared stream failing, and a liveness attestation 10 seconds later delivers no verification event to that stream (the declared stream receives one), while its receiver still holds active; once the suspension is delivered, liveness follows it. A requested verification waits behind a failed suspension delivery the same way. A verification also waits behind an earlier requested verification being retried, and behind a verification hand-off still in flight. requirements.text: When the joined party is a delegate rather than the Mission's `client_id`, the PDP MUST narrow the effective Authority Set to the delegable subset under the OAuth binding's per-entry `delegation` rules ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission}}): entries without a `delegation` member are excluded, `allowed_delegates` is applied, and `max_depth` is evaluated from the deployment's actor records rather than from a Mission-bound token's `act` chain.

observation.normative: evaluate() (step 4b) narrows a joined delegate's effective authority to entries carrying a join_delegation member whose allowed_delegates (when present) names that client; BOTH the deployment's DelegatePolicy.maxDepth ceiling AND each entry's own join_delegation.max_depth are compared against context.mission_join.delegate_depth, a REQUEST fact the PEP resolves fresh and carries onto the decision request (PepDeps.masJoin.resolveDelegateDepth), never a token act chain and never looked up by the PDP from static configuration (#557 review points 1, 3). The depth source is the deployment's own actor records (ActorRecords, services/mcp-payments/src/actor-records.ts): records are keyed on the canonical (issuer, id) pair, and resolveDepth walks delegated_by toward the Mission's own client_id (depth 0, adding 1 per hop), resolving ABSENT for no record, an unrooted chain, a cycle, or a chain that never reaches the Mission's client. An absent depth denies unconditionally on the delegate disposition, including where no max_depth is declared anywhere, per rule 5's own sentence: "A delegate with no actor record under the Mission is not recorded as acting under it, and the join fails `mission_binding_failed`." The hook the PEP resolves depth through takes the canonical (issuer, id) reference and the Mission's own client_id, both facts of the request the PEP already holds, so the ledger's resolver satisfies it with no issuer bound at construction: a record appended under one issuer is never consumed for a same-id Mission from another (#557 stage C2). The demo stack (src/demo/src/stack.ts) wires that ledger and seeds nothing into it, so every delegate join there denies until the deployment records an edge.

requirements.text: A permit under a join never exceeds any of three independently evaluated bounds: the authority the acting credential itself carries, the Mission's approved authority, and current Resource policy.

observation.normative: each of the three bounds denies ON ITS OWN with the other two satisfied, and all three satisfied permits, which is what makes them independently evaluated rather than one check wearing three names. Bound 1 is the acting credential's own authority (PepDeps.masJoin.resolveOrdinaryAuthority), checked on the facts the PEP establishes (resource, action, vendors, amount) before the PDP runs and carried to it as context.credential.authority; the joined Mission's view reaches the PDP unfiltered (D340), so a Mission entry broader than the credential still permits what the credential covers; absent, it cannot be honestly evaluated, so the joined route fails closed with out_of_authority rather than treating an unconfigured bound as unbounded. Bound 2 is the Mission's approved authority, matched by evaluate() against the joined authority set and checked through the Mission's contextual FGA projection (fga.checkWithContext), either of which denies out_of_authority. Bound 3 is current Resource policy, the ResourcePolicy bound to the decision point (#828), which denies resource_policy with both other bounds satisfied. The demo supplies a real bound-1 evaluator (src/demo/src/stack.ts): the credential's verified scope claim mapped through config/mas-join.json's scope_actions, so it models the token AS ISSUED and a narrower token yields a narrower permit for the same client
observation.local: bound 3's unit witness binds a refusing Resource-policy fixture to the decision point; the policy it stands for is the demo's stored OpenFGA entitlements (fgaResourcePolicy, #828), queried with the authenticated subject, client, action and targets and no Mission-derived input. The Mission's contextual FGA check stays part of bound 2. The MAS pilot (#818 slice 2) witnesses bound 3 end to end at its gateway with the stored OpenFGA policy rather than a fixture: revoking only the estate subject's entitlement denies resource_policy on a join the credential and Mission bounds still permit, and the policy is evaluated on the estate-authenticated subject and client, never on the Mission-side identities the mapping contract resolves, so the bound stays independent of the join

requirements.text: The PDP MUST record a joined-view commitment, `join_view_id`, as a top-level member of the Decision Evidence ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence}}) of every decision reached over a successful join, including one that policy then denies. It is separate from `policy_view_id`, which alone does not distinguish a joined decision from a direct one, and it is absent for a failed join and for a direct Mission-bound decision; the AuthZEN response carries no view identifier. `join_view_id` MUST change whenever the joining client identifier, the join disposition (the Mission's own `client_id` or an authorized delegate), or the resulting effective Authority Set differs, so a verifier can tell a joined decision's evidence from a direct Mission-bound decision's, and one joined view from a differently-joined one.

observation.normative: evaluate() (step 4b) records join_view_id (services/pdp/src/policy-view.ts's joinViewId) in a private per-evaluation JoinTrace once a baseline Join succeeds, and the PDP's Decision Evidence emitter signs it as a top-level member of the record (services/pdp/src/decision-evidence.ts), on the joined permit and on a later policy denial alike; the AuthZEN response context never carries it. A decision reached with no context.mission_join, or over a join that itself failed (mission_binding_failed, rule 6, no authoritySet ever exposed), records none. joinViewId's commitment is computed over the join disposition, the joining client_id, and the resolved (possibly delegate-narrowed) authoritySet, alongside the same (mission_id, mission_version, authority_hash, model_id) policyViewId already commits, so it changes whenever any of the three join-specific inputs differs
observation.local: join_view_id does not itself commit the acting subject: resolveBaselineJoin (mas-join.ts) requires byte-equality between the presented subject and the Mission's own view.subject as the join's own precondition (rule 3), so on any successful join the subject cannot differ from the Mission's own and adds nothing a separate commitment input would distinguish. The per-request recorded delegate depth is likewise not itself committed, only its filtering effect on the resolved authoritySet

requirements.notes: #249 implementation (D553, payments-runtime-profile-v13). The Operation Profile registry (kernel/operation-profile.ts) reads the version a carried reference names from its contract document, resolves the reference under the declared contract versions at admission and again at completion, and returns a refusal the transaction endpoint answers invalid_grant. Its refusals are witnessed at the registry (unit). Proved by admitting under the current version while ignoring the reference. #1846 (#249 C.2, D967): the registry is built from the declarations (contractOperationProfiles), the current version's profile registered and every other declared version's retained, so a resolving reference selects its own version's profile at the transaction endpoint: a Mission approved while 2026-10-26 was current is admitted and completes under payments-runtime-profile-v15, not v16. The registry holding only the current profile, as the shipped stack built it, refuses that reference at admission (the reproduction, kept as the control). A retired, out-of-retention or uncovered reference is refused by resolution, witnessed at the registry. Still partial: refusal of a non-resolving reference at admission and at completion is witnessed at the registry, not through the endpoint. Proved by mutation, each alone: retaining no older version, skipping retired versions, or registering every version as current fails a witness.

requirements.notes: Asserted: the re-decide arm. An entry-constrained approval permits schedule_payment against the invoice's current parameters (via pep.enforce()); the invoice is then mutated (reparameterization); presenting the identical, unchanged approval object to a FRESH pep.enforce() call denies action_approval_required, because evaluate()'s action-approval check recomputes parameter_digest fresh and compares it to the approval's stored digest -- and nothing executes on either call. NOT asserted: the anchor's TOCTOU-at-time-of-use clause -- reverifying the SAME single permitted attempt via Pep.reverify() immediately before execution, the way parameter-binding.must-bind-and-reverify does for an ordinary permit. That path is not reachable through any public server API for an approval-gated action: callWriteTool/callTransactionTool take no actionApproval parameter (only Pep.enforce() does, and it has no execution step of its own), and Pep.reverify() itself has no approval parameter at all -- it only re-checks the generic parameter_digest, with no notion of the approval object. Two calls to enforce() is the only approval-specific reverification this codebase's public surface offers.

requirements.notes: src/services/pdp/src/server.ts (PDP) and src/services/pdp/src/client.ts (PEP) are a genuinely separated topology over a real 127.0.0.1 HTTP hop, not another direct function call: the request and response are domain-separated HMAC'd end to end (src/services/pdp/src/channel-mac.ts), the PDP authenticates the PEP by a registered per-identity secret and accepts credential-derived inputs only from a PEP whose registered scopes include the request's audience, and the PEP authenticates the PDP by verifying the response MAC, bound to pep_id, nonce, request_issued_at, the request digest, HTTP status, and the response body, before trusting the decision it carries: a response validly signed for one request cannot be replayed as the answer to another. Every channel-boundary refusal is proven non-vacuous (evaluate() call count stays 0, via an injectable counter) and followed by a valid signed request on the SAME running server that permits. The co-resident case (mcp-payments/src/pep.ts calling evaluate() directly) is unaffected and is exercised separately to show it satisfies the requirement structurally. Not covered: mutual TLS as an alternative trust mode; wiring this channel into mcp-payments' own production PEP path (it remains a standalone reference adapter validating the contract, per the issue's own scoping). The raw-token-forwarding clause of this section is tracked separately as runtime.token-validation.raw-credential-not-used-outside-scope.

requirements.notes: The text carries two MUSTs: evaluate under the other type's own runtime semantics, and refuse if the PDP does not understand or cannot enforce them. The PDP recognizes exactly one authorization_details type (mission_resource_access), so it implements only the refusal limb, which is exactly this row's own observation.normative and assertion ("refusal"): recognition is a whitelist (@spec evaluate.ts step 5), so any other type never matches by resource/actions. Author-review finding 3 corrected WHICH refusal it falls through to: draft-mcguinness-mission-authzen.md's normative mapping table (@spec authzen#failure-condition-coverage) keeps "Action outside the Authority Set" (`out_of_authority`) and "Unsupported authorization_details type" (`unsupported_authorization_type`) as two different failure kinds, not two degrees of one; an entry matching this request's resource/actions under an unrecognized type is the second kind, so step 5 now denies unsupported_authorization_type there, reserving out_of_authority for a genuine absence of any matching entry regardless of type. The cited tests prove an unrecognized type and an absent type member both deny unsupported_authorization_type rather than pass through or misclassify as out_of_authority, a side-by-side case contrasting the two denial reasons on otherwise-identical requests, a mixed-authority_set case (an unrecognized-type entry alongside a valid entry for the same resource/actions) proving the unrecognized entry is skipped rather than short-circuiting the match (skip-not-shortcircuit unaffected by the classification fix), and a positive control (same file) proving the recognized-type case still permits. Defense in depth beyond evaluateInner's own check: AuthorityEntry.type is also a closed TypeScript literal ("mission_resource_access") both in policy-view.ts and in the AS kernel's own AuthorityEntry (src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/types.ts), and the transaction-authorization admission path separately refuses any other authorization_details type at admission (src/demo/src/stack.ts's operationProfiles comment: "an entry naming any other type is refused at admission rather than read structurally"); the whitelist check above is no longer relying solely on those upstream closures. requirements.notes: #828. The PDP now has an independent Resource-policy conjunct: a ResourcePolicy bound to the decision point, asked at evaluate() step 6b with the authenticated subject, client, action and targets and nothing Mission-derived, denying resource_policy. The unit truth table controls the Mission-authority and Resource-policy outcomes separately with named fixtures, and each cell was verified by disabling the step-6b refusal. A policy that cannot answer yields no decision, never a permit. Moved partial -> tested under #828's ledger rule, which required the real-OpenFGA assertion: the two OpenFGA citations (revoking only the stored entitlement denies resource_policy where the Mission permits, and restoring it permits; the Mission refusing denies where the entitlement permits) passed against a live OpenFGA in impl-ci at faf9250d.
