requirements.notes: Tested (#918, #1080, D333). Every reversible consequential write the deployment serves is witnessed at the resource operation: hold_transfer, the prepare phase of payments:payment.execute, resolves to the statement's consequential_write class default, single_use_decision_identifier, and its permit carries use_limit: 1 (D317, D333); schedule_payment and cancel_scheduled_payment resolve to their own validity_window_plus_idempotency_key declarations, a keyless request is refused by the PDP parameter_violation (and, at the resource operation, earlier at intake invalid_request with no PDP call, since the served schema requires the key; D316), and a keyed one is permitted under the short validity window (at most the published permit_validity_max_seconds, 300 s as shipped, 30 s under a 30 s maximum; #1028 review) with no use_limit and no claim. The PDP-level tests show the control follows the selected declaration, not the action name: an operation's own declaration is selected before the class default, so a class-wide key control removes the default, and an operation electing single use under a class-wide key default is permitted with use_limit: 1 and no key. The Enforcement Scope Statement publishes single_use_decision_identifier as the consequential_write class default (D333). The PEP consumes the single-use identifier on the unkeyed write path and reserves the key on the keyed path (runtime.idempotency.reversible-write-pep-reserve-and-retain); its refusal of a consumed identifier, on admission or retrieval under any key (D342), is runtime.single-use.reversible-write-refuse-second-presentation.

The clause applies wherever a single-use decision identifier is used; in this deployment that is every consequential_write the statement does not key (the published single_use_decision_identifier class default) and any keyed write whose permit carries use_limit. requirements.notes: Witnessed (#918): schedule_payment and cancel_scheduled_payment elect the idempotency-key control, and the enforcing PEP (mcp-payments-pep) reserves (idempotency scope, idempotency_key) in its own durable single-writer SQLite file (stores.pepWriteReservations.file), separate from the PDP claim domain and from transaction.ts. The schedule effect and its completed reservation and result commit in one local transaction, so eight concurrent attempts under one key that all found the pair free execute once and the other seven read the winner's record (concurrency). The record survives a close and reopen of the file, and is retained for the published P7D horizon: a retry after the 300 s permit expired resolves against it through its own fresh Decision, held to verifyPermitAtUse before release, without reaching admission, while the expired permit replayed into the effect step admits nothing; past the horizon the key is new. A changed operation conflicts, a fault inside the transaction leaves neither row, a fault after the commit resolves to the retained result, a reserved record is refused and never purged by time, and an unreachable store suppresses consumption_unavailable. This is a different store and mechanism from the high-consequence transaction-assurance tier; no transaction.ts test is cited. The reservation scope's actor is the shared stable identity (@mission/core idempotencyScopeActor, #1016 review): another instance of the same client, carried as an instance-profiled leaf, retries into the same scope and executes nothing new, and an instance-profiled leaf with no client to key on yields no scope, so the write is refused after its permit with no effect and no reservation, recorded under the deployment-defined error https://payments.demo/execution-errors/actor_unkeyable (caller-visible actor_unkeyable). The PDP caps each keyed write's permit at the published permit_validity_max_seconds, which the loader holds shorter than the retention, so no permit outlives its record: with a 30 s maximum and a 60 s retention, the original permit replayed after the record expired is refused permit_expired and nothing executes (#1028 review). #853 review: the reserved-or-completed record is retained across a declared change of boundary identifier: retrieval and the reservation transaction read it under the scope of every identifier the boundary replaces.

requirements.notes: Fail closed and surfaced; nothing is committed for later signing. Every post-permit refusal on the PEP's read, reversible-write and transaction paths, and enforcement's own post-permit refusals on all three, reads its suppressed disposition's result (#821, #1715): the refusal stands, nothing executes, and a record that cannot be written adds the gap and one operator alert. observation.local: the reference's one declared dependency (config/authority-dependencies.json: the Mission Subject's continuing delegation to the client acting under the Mission, governing user-delegated Missions, maximum staleness 300 s), observed by the identity-state resolver (packages/mission-core/src/authority-dependency.ts) over the configuration-backed identity source (config/identity.json's status and withdrawn_delegations), re-read without a restart; evaluated in the PDP's Resource-policy step (services/pdp/src/evaluate.ts step 6b) where the declaration routes direct evaluation to the PDP; a stale observation and a source that never answered are each a case of no acceptable observation remaining. The resolver dates each observation from when its read was issued, not when it completed, and publishes overlapping reads (a scheduled refresh, a reconciliation pass) in issue order, so a slow read never renews an old state's validity and an older read never replaces a newer one, a known withdrawal included (D813). Under lifecycle-only enforcement (no direct route) the PDP keeps the declared observation limits: the observation the last complete reconciliation acted on, older than max_staleness_seconds, refuses stale, and a failed latest read under a declared online check refuses unavailable; withdrawal and invalidation stay the reconciler's to commit. Each complete reconciliation also publishes the governed Missions whose recorded Subject its observation shows an applicable invalidation for (mapped to a lifecycle operation or not), and the lifecycle-only PDP refuses them withdrawn or invalidated, as direct evaluation would, whatever the Mission's state reads: an authorized resume while the Subject stays disabled restores nothing, and reliance returns only after a later complete pass observes the recovery and the Mission is active again. The set is recomputed by every complete pass and kept through a failed one. A pass classifies what its own observation shows through the same classification direct evaluation uses (classifyObservedInvalidation): the source's current availability and the observation's age are never taken as an invalidation gone, and a pass that cannot classify a governed Mission publishes nothing.

the credential's discharge and approval conditions are decided at the PDP (D312) > never borrows another Mission entry's live state: any discharged source refuses, whatever the entry order (#1133 review P1)

the credential's discharge and approval conditions are decided at the PDP (D312) > refuses a credential discharge condition unless the view proves it holds the committed Authority Set (#1133 re-review P1)

requirements.notes: Discharge state is kept per Mission entry digest, never per condition, so two entries carrying one condition can differ in state; the credential entry is therefore resolved to every entry it could derive from, and one discharged among them refuses even when another is live, since the PDP cannot tell which one the credential derives from (#1133 review P1). A view built from an effective set (Status and introspection omit discharged entries) need not hold every entry the credential could derive from, so it cannot establish the condition; a PDP fed such a view refuses every discharge-conditioned credential entry, the fail-closed reading (#1133 re-review, D335). The proof covers the set, not the discharge delta, whose completeness stays the loader's obligation (#1144).

requirements.notes: #1276 (D457) specification slice. The reference PDP and PEPs do not carry or match operation_target yet; #1276's implementation step owns the witness. Expected outcomes: vectors/mission-authzen/operation-target.json. #1276 implementation (D457, payments-runtime-profile-v6). The remote PDP refuses a target outside the authenticated PEP's enforcement scope before evaluation (P10, endpoint). Absent, malformed and ambiguous targets are refused before evaluation at evaluate() only (P5, unit). Mutations M3b, M9 and M19 fail P5, P10 and P6. #1296 review: "one absolute URI" is checked as RFC 3986 absolute-URI syntax (Section 4.3; every % begins a pct-encoded triplet, Section 2.1) by an ABNF transcription in isOperationTarget, plus RFC 9110's non-empty http(s) host, never by new URL(), which accepts %zz, a trailing % and %4. Mutations (new URL() only; pct-encoded loosened to {0,2}, {1,2} or a trailing %; the host rule removed) fail that witness. Partial stays: the non-string, array and no-fallback clauses are witnessed at evaluate() only (P5). #1276 argument-derived contracts: a remote PEP may be registered for operation contracts (AuthorizedPep.operationContracts); the remote PDP admits every target a registered contract establishes and refuses, before evaluation, the service identifier when only an argument-derived contract is registered, a second segment, a non-canonical encoding, a dot-segment and another collection, as operation_target_invalid. requirements.notes: #1629 (D744 ruling 3). The PDP checks action_phase in evaluate(), after the operation target: an out-of-set value (unknown, case, padding, empty, null, number, array, object) and a missing phase for an action its trusted operation declaration places at phases are refused before evaluation as phase_invalid, with no decision, no Decision Evidence, no FGA check and no Resource policy query, in process and over the remote channel. The trusted declaration is the PDP-side phasedActions binding (EvaluateOptions, the decision point and the remote server), stripped from a caller's options. The shipped demo stack binds no phasedActions, so its PDP declares no phased action and refuses only an out-of-set phase; binding the catalog's compound actions there is a deployment follow-up. Mutations: not refusing an out-of-set phase fails the out-of-set, signed-record, remote and evaluate-decision witnesses; ignoring the declaration fails the missing-phase, signed-record, decision-point and remote witnesses; keeping a caller's declaration at the decision point fails the decision-point witness; the remote server not applying its own declaration fails the remote witness.

requirements.notes: Re-quoted at #1629 (D744 ruling 8): the effective-deny clause is its own row, authzen.obligation-processing.effective-deny. Tested at #1640: the payments PEP performs the AuthZEN Obligations Profile's notification through its configured transport, every witness over HTTP with DPoP. On a permit it completes the transmission before releasing the effect: for a keyed write and for an irreversible commit, no schedule or wire exists when the transmission completes, and the completed record names the obligation fulfilled. A notification it cannot fulfill (a failed transmission, a malformed instance, no transport configured) releases nothing. On a denial it still denies (out_of_authority, nothing scheduled, no Execution Evidence) and transmits the returned notification. Mutations: treating the permit's obligations as fulfilled without performing them fails the fulfilment, irreversible-commit and cannot-perform witnesses; not awaiting the transmission fails both before-release witnesses; counting a failed transmission as fulfilled fails the cannot-perform witness; skipping the denial's obligations fails the denial witness; letting a denial carrying obligations take the permit path fails both denial witnesses. D770 ruling 6: a denial whose Decision Evidence does not verify still stands, still transmits its notification and carries evidence_gap decision_evidence_unverifiable, with nothing retained or recorded; a denial carried by a response that fails channel authentication is refused channel_failure and transmits nothing. Mutations: skipping the denial's obligations when its evidence did not verify fails the unverifiable-evidence witness; dropping the evidence gap fails it too, and reporting the gap on every denial fails the verified denial witness; accepting an unauthenticated channel response fails the channel witness, and with its refusal assertion removed the nothing-transmitted assertion alone fails.

requirements.notes: #1629 (D744 ruling 8); tested at #1640. Over HTTP with DPoP, a permit carrying an obligation type the PEP does not implement, a step-up it cannot perform, a notification it cannot fulfill (a failed transmission, a malformed instance, no transport configured), or a notification beside an unrecognized obligation is refused unfulfillable_obligation with no protected effect (nothing scheduled, no reservation, no consumed permit) and a suppressed obligation_unfulfilled record naming each outcome; the same permit with no obligation schedules. Mutations: ignoring a non-array member fails the witness, and with the refusal assertion removed the no-effect assertion alone fails; giving a non-array member an empty outcome list fails it.

requirements.notes: #1629 (D744 ruling 5): the AuthZEN profile's copy (authzen.transport.no-double-charge-on-retry) is removed in favor of this home. The reference meters two bounds. Duration lease (#1440): a keyed request retried under the same idempotency key, sequentially or concurrently, opens one activity leased by one permit, and a keyed renewal retried under its key extends the lease once, settled or not; committing the lease on a retransmission fails all three duration witnesses, and committing it on a suppressed duplicate fails the first two. max_budget (#816, D830 ruling 6, closing the max_budget half of #1660; impl/816-budget-reservations 22c1fae0): a retry and a replay under the same key, before and after a completed settlement, a retry after a lost permit response, a retry adopting a claim abandoned by a crash before its decision persisted, and a duplicate commit-phase request each reserve once on both counters (reserving again on a suppressed retry, Z5, fails the replay, lost-response and phase witnesses; dropping the metered cache bypass, B, fails the lost-response witness; keeping an abandoned claim's reservation at boot, R2, fails the crash witness). The decision-identifier half for max_budget is the settlement keyed on evaluation_id: a redelivered completed settlement commits once (re-applying a duplicate, T8d, fails it). requirements.text: MUST extend at least to the Mission's `expires_at`, so a duplicate the Mission could still admit always resolves against the recorded key

observation.normative: a duplicate of a metered payment presented at any time before the Mission's expires_at resolves against its recorded idempotency claim and draws nothing further on either counter
observation.local: The reference never purges a metered claim by time (the stored decision is tombstoned after the window; the row and its reservations stay), so a same-Mission duplicate meets the claim for the Mission's whole life, and a terminal Mission is refused mission_inactive before the claim step. The idempotency scope keeps the Mission (D907): an Expansion successor's same-key re-presentation takes a new claim while continuing the same budget counters. The payments ledger's one-settlement-per-invoice rule is a separate duplicate guard, not lineage-wide idempotency: within a process it refuses the wire and the duplicate reservation is released; across a restart the in-memory ledger is the documented limit.

The capability stays disabled and unclaimed. Slice 3b (62325958) adds a backstop, not this refusal: a Mission recorded as a Child Mission anywhere in a standing-payment lineage derives no budget binding and is refused at the PDP. Slice 3a (impl/813-standing-payment-admission at a7063aab): in the reference only a standing-payment lineage carries max_budget, and a Child Mission under its instance is refused delegation_not_permitted. Mutation: removing the child guard fails it (refused not_strict_subset instead). Slice 4 AS track (impl/813-as-slice4 at 03a9a4a6, D877): at /token a Child Mission requested from a standing-payment instance, and from its expansion successor holding a children grant, is refused delegation_not_permitted and creates nothing. Mutation: removing the child guard (29) fails both only through the reason (not_strict_subset). D947 gap 2 (impl/813-child-refusal-witness at aa542b79): that child omitted delegation, so derivation gave it the policy ceiling's grant (max_depth 2, five children of depth 2), broader than the successor's (max_depth 1, two children of depth 1), and the strict-subset proof refused it with or without the guard. The new witnesses, at the kernel and at /token, send a child that restates the successor's per-payment bound, vendor and children grant, for a child actor the grant admits: under the successor, which carries the instance's max_budget, it is refused delegation_not_permitted (the kernel witness asserts the guard's own message), no grant is issued and nothing is created (Mission count and findChildren unchanged). On the dispatched instance itself no child is admissible without the guard either: the instance holds no delegation grant (a standing-payment ceiling admits none, refused at consent and re-checked at dispatch), so a derived child entry introduces the policy ceiling's grant (not_strict_subset) or lacks the children on-switch (delegation_not_permitted), and no single-layer mutant admits a child there; the instance witnesses prove ordering and reason. Tested: the successor is a Mission carrying max_budget, and each clause (refused, nothing created) is asserted and killed by a mutant that leaves every other layer in place. D877 ruling 1 keeps this refusal a tested prerequisite. The successor case covers a Mission carrying max_budget other than the dispatched instance.

requirements.text: continue the counters of the Mission they replace: consumption to date carries forward, and the successor's bound caps the cumulative consumption of the chain

observation.normative: an Expansion successor's metered actions draw on the counter its predecessor used: consumption to date carries forward, and the successor's max_budget caps the chain's cumulative consumption instead of opening a fresh balance
observation.local: design decision a: the instance counter is keyed by the first Mission of the successor chain, counter_scope mission. A successor keeps the dispatched instance's max_budget exactly: assertSuccessorMaxBudget (kernel/standing-payment.ts), called by createExpansion (kernel/expansion.ts) and createCeilingDrawdownInCallerTx (kernel/progressive.ts), refuses a successor Intent whose max_budget differs in amount or currency or is absent, and standingPaymentBudgetBindingOf derives underivable (denied constraint_unsupported at the PDP) for a Mission whose max_budget differs from the instance's. The successor's bound is therefore the bound the chain's instance counter is limited by; a successor bound that differs from its predecessor's does not arise.

requirements.notes: #816, D830. The capability stays disabled and unclaimed. A carryover replacement cannot arise while children are refused. Also homes the template's 'its successors continue its budget counters' for the instance counter. Slice 2 (#816, impl/816-budget-reservations 22c1fae0, decision point over a real claim-domain file): a successor bound to its predecessor's first Mission draws on the same mission counter: the same counter_id, 200.00 remaining of a 500.00 max_budget after 300.00, and a 200.00 payment fills it. Keying the instance counter by the successor's own Mission id (T8f) fails it; so do removing the reservation (A1) and refusing at equality (T8a). Slice 3b (impl/813-budget-binding-3b at 62325958): through the composed stack an expansion successor's payment draws on the dispatched instance's mission counter with its consumption to date (refused beyond the 25.00 left of 150.00, then permitted to exhaust it); keying the successor's binding by its own id (U2) or deriving it unbound (U1) opens a fresh balance or none, and dropping the instance limit (Q3p) lets the chain exceed its cap, each failing the witness. A successor's max_budget equals its predecessor's (observation.local, D877), and the AS witness of the refusal of an unequal one is 'refuses an expansion successor of a standing-payment instance that changes or drops its max_budget (#813)' (template-standing-payment.test.ts). D961: that refusal does not make ordinary continuation unreachable, so it is witnessed directly (impl/813-proof-runtime at 5a44a14e) at the decision point: createDecisionPoint's budgetBindings source answers the instance msn_a and its successor msn_a2 with the one binding rooted at msn_a (max_budget 500.00). The predecessor's 300.00 completes; the successor, whose caller view carries a fresh binding rooted at itself, is refused quota_exceeded for 300.00 on the predecessor's mission counter with 200.00 remaining, is permitted 200.00 on that counter and the shared one, and its completed settlement commits 500.00 on both; a further 0.01 is refused on the mission counter at 0.00 remaining while the shared counter keeps 500.00; no counter keyed by msn_a2 exists. Re-rooting the charge at the successor's own id (S2i: budgetCharge's binding replaced by { ...binding, instance: { ...binding.instance, root_mission_id: view.id } } in evaluate.ts), an unbounded instance limit (S2ii: the mission counter's limitMinor: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER in resolveBudgetCharge), metering the caller's presented binding (S2iii: attachBudgetBinding returns the view when it carries one) and dropping every binding (S2iv: attachBudgetBinding returns the view unbound) each fail it; with every assertion before it removed, S2i and S2iii each fail the no-successor-counter assertion alone. Tested.

D961 (impl/813-proof-runtime at 5a44a14e): a second witness runs the intake over the deployment's own key resolver, buildBoundaryEvidenceKeyResolver (services/pdp/src/enforcement-boundary.ts, as the composed stack wires it), with this PEP's key published for this boundary and emitter only and a second boundary in the declaration. A record with no evidence_envelope member, one signed under this PEP's key claiming the other boundary's audience, and one naming another emitter are each refused with both reservations reserved and both counters unchanged, and the record bound as published commits. Accepting an unenveloped record (I5a: settle treats a record without evidence_envelope as verified), resolving the key by kid across every boundary whatever the audience (I5b) and dropping the emitter comparisons from the resolver (I5c) each fail it at their case's refusal and, with that refusal assertion removed, at the unchanged-counters assertion alone. #1841 (D974; fix/1841-settlement-audience at c41a03f7, mutation at the same commit): the audience case's second reading is refused. A record validly signed under another boundary's published key, bound to that boundary's audience and emitter, naming this permit's evaluation_id and delivered by the permit's own PEP, settles nothing: settle compares the authenticated record's audience byte for byte with the boundary retained for the permit's claim (runtime-evidence#execution-evidence-object, the audience member) before any effect, so the claim's settlement, a conflicting record's retention, alarm and commit, the late budget correction and the redemption owner's query are all behind it. The boundary is retained on the claim (claim schema 6), written at the claim and at adoption; the scope cannot serve, since a claim adopted through a replaced identifier's scope (#853) keeps that scope. A pre-6 row takes the audience its stored permit's Decision Evidence recorded; a row without one keeps NULL and settles nothing. Four other boundaries publish their own keys in one declaration (another port, the identifier with an upper-case host, the identifier with a trailing slash, the identifier truncated to its origin). Their records are refused audience_mismatch for completed, failed and suppressed outcomes on an unsettled claim (the failed and suppressed ones named by the redemption owner as the redeeming attempt), for a conflicting completed record, the applied attempt's suppressed record and a redelivery of the applied record's members after an applied failed settlement, and for a completed record after an incorrect operator release past the window. Each leaves the claim row, its transitions, the conflict table, the reservations and both counters unchanged and raises no alert, the unsettled claim's failed and suppressed records never reach the redemption owner, and the permit's own boundary's record settles in each case. The adoption witness settles a claim adopted across a declared change at the adopting permit's boundary and refuses the replaced identifier's record; the legacy-file witness upgrades a schema 5 file and refuses a NULL-boundary row's own conflicting record and a record whose claim row is gone. Mutants, each alone with the source restored: removing the comparison (M1) fails all seven at their refusal; moving it after the claim's settlement (M2) fails six, and after the late correction (M3) all seven, at the unchanged-state assertion alone; moving it after the redemption owner's query (M4) fails the failed and suppressed witnesses at the never-asked assertion; a case-insensitive (M5), record-prefix (M6), boundary-prefix (M7) or URL-normalized (M8) comparison fails the five boundary witnesses; treating a NULL boundary as a match (M9) or as the scope's audience (M10), dropping the backfill (M11) and letting a record with no claim row reach the correction (M12) fail the legacy-file witness; leaving the boundary unchanged at adoption (M13) or comparing the scope's audience (M14) fails the adoption witness; omitting the boundary at the claim (M15) fails six. Rerun with every witness assertion soft, each refusal, unchanged-state, conflict-table, never-asked and alert assertion fails on its own under at least one of M1 to M4 and M9 to M14.

requirements.notes: #816, D830. The capability stays disabled and unclaimed. Also homes the settlement-states 'Conflicting settlement' item. Slice 4 (#816, D877; impl/816-pdp-slice4 at 793d2e85, mutation on impl/816-pdp-track at eeb034e5, the same commits): a record conflicting with the applied settlement (a second execution_id, or the applied attempt with another outcome) is refused already_settled, never acknowledged as the duplicate, leaves the applied claim settlement unchanged (read from the claim file), is retained once per distinct record, and raises one settlement_conflict alarm, also on the composed stack's alert path; a redelivered conflict retains and alarms nothing new. Once a settlement is applied, a non-completed record reaches the conflict check whatever the redemption owner answers and moves no counter; an applied failed record's later same-attempt suppressed record leaves the reservation held; a conflicting completed record commits a held or released reservation only from the permit's own PEP and epoch, and never one released because no permit left the PDP. Not retaining (X2), not alarming (X3), not committing a conflicting completed (X4), overwriting the applied settlement (X5; MD on the stack), re-alarming a redelivery (X6), moving counters for a non-completed conflict (X7, alone), acknowledging the same attempt's other outcome as a duplicate (X1), keeping the redeemer gate on a settled claim (RF1), committing only released reservations (MC), applying a non-completed conflict's own effect (ME), dropping the epoch or no-permit guard (RF5a, RF5b, RF5c), keying retention without the error (RF7) and leaving the stack's alarm unwired (X8) each fail their witness. #1771 review (D907; impl/816-pdp-slice4 at 7bb6835e, with the failed record's replaced-error case at 4c237470 and the null-error normalization at c136037a; mutation rerun at c136037a): the claim keeps the applied record's error, so the applied attempt with the same outcome and another error is a conflict too. An applied suppressed record's changed error, and an applied failed record's error added where it carried none or replaced by another, are each refused already_settled, never acknowledged as the duplicate, retained and alarmed once, with the applied settlement, its stored error and the counters unchanged; an identical redelivery carrying an error is acknowledged as the duplicate and retains and alarms nothing. Dropping the error from the duplicate check (M1) fails the first two, and at 4c237470, with that case run first, fails the replaced-error case on its own; storing NULL instead of the applied error (M2), or leaving the error out of the settling UPDATE (M3, the same stored state), fails all three; storing an empty string for an absent error (M4) fails the second; treating a stored NULL as matching any error (M5) fails the second alone. Partial: a redelivery that differs from the applied record only in a metering entry is still acknowledged as the duplicate, because the reference's settlement reads the attempt, outcome and error and ignores a metering member (its Execution Evidence carries none).

requirements.text: a reservation MUST carry a bounded lease

observation.normative: every budget reservation is recorded with a finite lease
observation.local: A budget reservation has no lease column of its own: it is written in its idempotency claim's transaction (budget_reservations, keyed by evaluation_id) and takes that claim's lease, the permit's valid_until plus the action class's declared execution_lease_max_seconds (leaseMaxMs in services/pdp/src/idempotency-claims.ts; 30 s for irreversible_action in the shipped transaction_assurance declaration). requirements.text: An idempotent action class makes a retry safe, not the first attempt void, and reversing a reversible action is a compensation action

observation.normative: neither a successful retry nor a compensating payment reversal releases or refunds the original payment's reservation or committed amount
observation.local: The PDP meters a budget-bound Mission's payment by context.amount. A retry under the payment's key is suppressed duplicate_suppressed and reserves nothing, whether the payment's reservation is reserved, held or committed; a retry under a new key is a new operation charged afresh, and its completion leaves the first attempt's reservation held. A compensate-phase request carrying an amount, which is what the reference PEP's reversal crossing sends, is refused constraint_unsupported (decision h) and claims nothing, so a priced reversal of a budget-bound payment is unsupported and never executes. A compensate-phase request missing its metering projection (context.amount absent while its normalized parameters still carry the amount) is permitted and claimed under its own key, charging nothing, and synthetic completed evidence for it settles its own claim only; this demonstrates no zero-cost or executable payment reversal; a later non-execution record for the reversed payment is a conflicting settlement. After each, the payment's claim keeps its own settlement and its reservations and both counters are unchanged.

requirements.notes: #816, D830. The capability stays disabled and unclaimed. Slice 4 (#816, D877; impl/816-pdp-slice4 at 793d2e85, mutation on impl/816-pdp-track at eeb034e5, the same commits): after a completed 300.00 payment, a retry under its key is suppressed duplicate_suppressed and a compensate request naming it is refused constraint_unsupported; both reservations stay committed, with 300.00 committed on the shared counter. Releasing a completed payment on its retry (W14) fails it. D974 (impl/816-compensation-proof at a2815d9b; every mutant ran there, alone, in its own process group, with the source restored after): the reachable retry and compensation paths are exercised, so the row is not classified as unexercised. Two further witnesses: after a completed 300.00 payment, a retry under its key, a reversal carrying the amount (the reversal action and the metered action's own compensate phase) refused constraint_unsupported, a repeat of it, a reversal decided without an amount that executes and settles its own claim, a suppressed record for the payment, and a retry after each leave the payment's reservations committed and 300.00 committed on the shared and mission counters, its claim completed on its own record; while a payment's outcome is unknown, a retry under its key and a refused reversal leave its reservation reserved, then held once its lease elapses, and a retry under a new key that completes commits its own 300.00 while the first attempt stays held on both counters. Each distinguishing mutant is killed: a completed payment released on its retry (K1); a retry taken as a fresh unexecuted operation that releases and re-reserves (K2), re-reserves only (K2b), or does so only after the compensation request missing its metering projection (K2c); a retry releasing a reserved (K3a) or held (K3b) reservation; a retry under a new key releasing the first attempt at its claim (K7a) or on its completion (K7b); a refused reversal releasing the payment's reservation, completed or open (K4a), refunding both counters (K4b), or settling the payment's claim as not executed (K4c); synthetic completed evidence for that compensation request releasing the payment (K5a), refunding its counters (K5b) or settling its claim as not executed (K5c); a non-execution record after the reversal releasing the payment (K6a) or settling its claim as not executed (K6b). With the earlier failing assertions removed, the counter assertions alone kill K1, K2b, K3a, K4b, K5b, K7a and K7b, and the mission counter alone kills K1, K4b and K5b. Unsupported, stated and not enabled: a successful compensation carrying the payment's amount, which is the reference PEP's reverse_wire_transfer request, is refused under decision h, so the reference never executes a priced reversal of a budget-bound payment and keeps no compensation accounting (a reversal never credits the budget). The witness's compensation request is missing its metering projection (context.amount deleted while the normalized parameters still carry the amount) and is followed by synthetic completed evidence; it demonstrates no zero-cost or executable payment reversal, and the reference PEP's priced reversal stays unsupported (D991). Tested.

an obligation the PEP does not recognize or cannot fulfill is an effective deny at the resource's HTTP endpoint (@spec authzen#obligation-processing, authzen#obligations, #1629) > a permit carrying an unrecognized or unfulfillable obligation releases no protected effect over HTTP with DPoP: the write is refused unfulfillable_obligation, nothing is scheduled, and the permit's disposition is suppressed obligation_unfulfilled; the same permit with no obligation schedules

every consequential permit's final disposition is one Execution Evidence record at the resource's HTTP endpoint (@spec authzen#execution-evidence-requirement, authzen#conformance, #1640) > a completed consequential read (get_invoice, list_invoices, lookup_vendor) over HTTP with DPoP releases its result with exactly one signed completed Execution Evidence record linked to the permit's evaluation

every consequential permit's final disposition is one Execution Evidence record at the resource's HTTP endpoint (@spec authzen#execution-evidence-requirement, authzen#conformance, #1640) > a completed reversible write under a single-use permit (hold_transfer) over HTTP with DPoP releases the hold with exactly one signed completed Execution Evidence record linked to the permit's evaluation

every consequential permit's final disposition is one Execution Evidence record at the resource's HTTP endpoint (@spec authzen#execution-evidence-requirement, authzen#conformance, #1640) > a completed keyed reversible write (schedule_payment) over HTTP with DPoP schedules once with exactly one signed completed Execution Evidence record linked to the permit's evaluation

every consequential permit's final disposition is one Execution Evidence record at the resource's HTTP endpoint (@spec authzen#execution-evidence-requirement, authzen#conformance, #1640) > a completed irreversible commit (execute_wire_transfer) or external commitment (send_remittance_email) over HTTP with DPoP commits one connector effect with exactly one signed completed Execution Evidence record linked to the permit's evaluation, recorded by the executor at the commit point

every consequential permit's final disposition is one Execution Evidence record at the resource's HTTP endpoint (@spec authzen#execution-evidence-requirement, authzen#conformance, #1640) > a read or a hold whose completed record cannot be recorded over HTTP with DPoP returns no protected data: no response byte carries the result, the refusal is evidence_unavailable, and the permit's disposition is recorded suppressed

every consequential permit's final disposition is one Execution Evidence record at the resource's HTTP endpoint (@spec authzen#execution-evidence-requirement, authzen#conformance, #1640) > a keyed write whose effect committed but whose completed record cannot be recorded over HTTP with DPoP reports the emission_failed gap with no result on the wire: the schedule stands once, and a retry under the same key retrieves it under its own permit

requirements.notes: Re-quoted at #1629 (D744 ruling 2): the transaction-assurance-class restriction is removed, an expansion, so earlier coverage does not transfer. Tested at #1640, every witness over HTTP with DPoP: a pre-decision refusal emits a signed Refusal Record (phase_unavailable). A completed consequential read (get_invoice, list_invoices, lookup_vendor), a completed reversible write (hold_transfer under a single-use permit, schedule_payment under an idempotency key) and a completed irreversible commit or external commitment (execute_wire_transfer, send_remittance_email) each emit exactly one signed completed record linked to the permit's evaluation, carrying both parameter digests where the permit binds one; a suppressed consequential write emits a suppressed record (obligation_unfulfilled). The reference emits no failed outcome. The Decision Base exemption is a permission with no observable duty. Durable evidence reservation stays the transaction-assurance requirement's (D744 ruling 2). Mutations: skipping the phase check fails the refusal witness; dropping the completed record on the read path, the unkeyed write path, the keyed write path or the transaction path fails that path's witness and no other completed-record witness; skipping the obligation check fails the suppression witness. D770 ruling 4: when the completed record cannot be recorded, a read or a hold, which disclosed nothing, is refused evidence_unavailable with its disposition recorded suppressed under a deployment error name, and no response byte over HTTP with DPoP carries the result; a keyed write whose local transaction committed reports gap emission_failed with no result on the wire, and a retry under its key retrieves the result. Mutations: releasing the result on the read path or the unkeyed write path fails the withholding witness, and with the parsed-response assertion removed the response-bytes assertion alone fails; returning the keyed write's result with the gap fails the keyed witness, again on the bytes alone; not recording the withheld result's suppression fails the withholding witness.

requirements.text: A PDP conforming to the Decision Base MUST:

observation.normative: a conforming PDP refuses an in-scope request lacking Mission decision context and performs the consistency checks, classifies every denial per the runtime-denial-classification, returns the full decision context, and advertises the mission-runtime capability URN; emitting the runtime evidence companion's records is a Runtime Evidence profile duty, not a Decision Base one (#703)

requirements.text: A PDP additionally claiming the Runtime Evidence profile ({{profiles-and-capabilities}}) MUST emit the records of {{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence}} for every decision, and a Refusal Record for an in-scope request it refuses before evaluation

observation.normative: a PDP claiming the Runtime Evidence profile emits the runtime evidence companion's records, including a Refusal Record, for every decision and pre-evaluation refusal; a PDP claiming only the Decision Base records decisions and refusals in its own internal form (#703, closing the unconditional-adoption-gate defect #703 identified)

requirements.text: A compromised or misconfigured Access Request Service can auto-approve escalations, so it MUST be trusted, authenticated, and access-controlled like the PDP, and its auto-approval is bounded as {{requestable-denials}} specifies.

observation.normative: the Access Request Service is trusted, authenticated, and access-controlled to the same standard as the PDP

requirements.text: The PDP endpoint MUST be served over TLS 1.2 or later (TLS 1.3 RECOMMENDED). PEP-to-PDP authentication MUST be mutual, satisfying the integrity and mutual-authentication requirement the runtime profile places on the PEP-PDP channel

observation.normative: the PDP endpoint is served over TLS 1.2 or later, and PEP-to-PDP authentication is mutual

requirements.text: The PEP SHOULD minimize the denial detail it relays to the agent; a generic refusal suffices to stop the action, and the full reason and contributing constraints belong in evidence, not in the agent-facing response.

observation.normative: the PEP relays a minimized, generic denial to the agent-facing surface, keeping the full denial reason and contributing constraints in evidence rather than the agent response, and a deployment rate-limits access requests per Mission to bound denial-oracle probing

requirements.text: A PDP conforming to the Decision Base MUST advertise the full URN `urn:ietf:params:authzen:mission-runtime`, never the bare capability name.

observation.normative: a conforming PDP's metadata capabilities array advertises the full urn:ietf:params:authzen:mission-runtime URN for the Decision Base, never the bare capability name

requirements.notes: The base AuthZEN Authorization API 1.0 is pinned in notes/external-pins.json (id AUTHZEN, openid/authzen commit 2b07366d2dfd7ad9e2dedf44b97bd41e8a2b8c63, status established at Ship 3), so this row's upstream registry surface is verifiable against that snapshot.

requirements.text: A PDP that additionally conforms to a feature profile MUST advertise that profile's own capability URN as well; a PDP MUST NOT advertise a feature-profile URN it does not conform to.

observation.normative: a PDP's advertised capabilities array carries a feature-profile URN if and only if the PDP actually conforms to that feature profile

requirements.text: A PEP MUST NOT rely on a feature profile whose URN the PDP's advertised `capabilities` does not include: an unadvertised profile fails closed exactly as an absent one does elsewhere in this document ({{profiles-and-capabilities}}).

observation.normative: a PEP treats a feature profile absent from the PDP's advertised capabilities the same as a profile the deployment never composed: it fails closed rather than assuming the profile's behavior

requirements.text: Capability advertisement is PDP-declared, never requester-selected: nothing in a PEP's request selects, enables, or negotiates a feature profile, and a requester cannot omit a required profile to downgrade enforcement ({{profiles-and-capabilities}}).

observation.normative: no PEP request member selects, enables, or negotiates a feature profile; profile composition is fixed by deployment/PDP configuration, not by anything the requester supplies on a given request

requirements.text: A binding MUST define a Mission Reference that is:

observation.normative: the Mission Reference is stable for the lifetime and retention period of the Mission Context, unambiguous within the declared Controller namespace, and never reassigned to a different Mission Context within that namespace

requirements.text: If the native reference is not globally unambiguous, the binding MUST define the Controller identifier or other namespace value with which it is compared.

observation.normative: when the reference alone is not globally unambiguous, the binding names the namespace value compared alongside it

requirements.text: A reference disclosed beyond the Controller MUST NOT be guessable by parties outside the Mission's authorized set

observation.normative: a disclosed reference resists guessing by unauthorized parties: satisfied by at least 128 bits of reference entropy, a reference derived from undisclosed content, or a namespace whose every keyed surface authenticates the caller and does not disclose existence

tests.name: mission reference unguessability (@spec mission-substrate#reference) > the Mission Reference's random component carries at least 128 bits of entropy
mission reference unguessability (@spec mission-substrate#reference) > newMissionId draws at least 18 bytes (144 bits) from a caller-injected random source
mission reference unguessability (@spec mission-substrate#reference) > newMissionId's default source is node:crypto's randomBytes and needs no argument
mission reference unguessability (@spec mission-substrate#reference) > successive draws are distinct (sanity check, not a substitute for the entropy proof above)
mission reference unguessability (@spec mission-substrate#reference) > the four known msn_ minting sites all call the single newMissionId helper
mission reference unguessability (@spec mission-substrate#reference) > no file in kernel/ other than mission-id.ts itself constructs an msn_ id inline

requirements.notes: Length alone is not entropy, so Mission ID generation is now centralized into one helper (src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/mission-id.ts's newMissionId), built on node:crypto's randomBytes, and all four msn_ minting sites (kernel.ts insertRecord, expansion.ts, child-delegation.ts, template.ts) were updated to call it instead of constructing the id inline. The helper itself is tested directly: one test injects an observing wrapper around the source function and asserts the helper requests exactly MISSION_ID_ENTROPY_BYTES (18, 144 bits, above the 128-bit floor this row's normative text names as one of three satisfying conditions), proving the entropy claim is about the source and byte count, not merely the length of one identifier from one call site; a second test exercises the default parameter (node:crypto's randomBytes with no argument supplied), decodes the exact byte count, AND reads mission-id.ts's own source to confirm the default is bound to the imported node:crypto randomBytes, not a same-named local; a distinctness sanity check over 1000 draws is additional, not a substitute for the entropy proof. The last two tests close the site-coverage class, not just four known instances: one confirms each known site calls newMissionId(), the other scans every file in kernel/ (not a fixed list) and asserts none but mission-id.ts itself still constructs `msn_${...}` inline, so a fifth minting site added later in a new file would still be caught. No negative-class row exists anywhere in the manifest for the mission-reference surface, so that half of the per-surface minimum is not expressible from this manifest as authored.

requirements.text: The binding MUST define how a relying component identifies the Controller responsible for the reference.

observation.normative: a relying component has a defined mechanism (local configuration, protocol identifier, trust anchor, or other substrate-native mechanism) for identifying the accountable Controller

requirements.text: A binding MUST NOT describe a bare value as globally identifying a Mission when its uniqueness actually depends on unstated local context.

observation.normative: a reference whose uniqueness depends on unstated local context is not documented as globally identifying

requirements.text: a provider statement MUST NOT use colocation to imply that one role's assertion establishes another role's fact

observation.normative: co-locating roles in one implementation never lets one role's assertion silently stand in for a different role's fact in the provider statement

requirements.text: At approval, the Controller MUST bind the Mission Context to the Actor identity, key, workload identity, authenticated session, or other actor handle defined by the binding.

observation.normative: the Controller binds the Mission Context to a defined Actor handle at approval

tests.name: actor binding at approval (@spec mission-substrate#actor-binding) > binds the Mission Context to the client_id Actor handle at approval, and the binding round-trips unchanged

requirements.notes: kernel.approve()'s clientId input is the substrate's Actor handle per the family crosswalk (PLAN.md D85 BUNDLE 3: client_id maps to Actor); it is persisted on MissionRecord.client_id and round-trips through kernel.get unchanged. This is the client-Actor binding, distinct from the existing approval_basis tests (mission#approval-basis), which cover the consenting human (Approver), a different substrate role.

requirements.text: The value MUST be derived from authenticated context or verified proof; it MUST NOT be accepted solely from an unauthenticated proposal.

observation.normative: the Actor handle comes from authenticated context or verified proof; an unauthenticated proposal alone never establishes it

requirements.text: The binding MUST state:

observation.normative: the binding states what the Actor handle identifies, how the Controller establishes it at approval, and how a later positive governance decision establishes that the acting party is the bound Actor or an authorized delegate

requirements.text: A binding that maps between identifiers MUST define which component performs the mapping and the assurance and ambiguity of that mapping.

observation.normative: a binding that maps between identifier syntaxes names the mapping component and states the mapping's assurance and ambiguity

requirements.text: The binding MUST maintain either the Approved Context itself or a verifiable commitment to it.

observation.normative: the binding maintains either the Approved Context or a verifiable commitment to it

tests.name: approved context commitment (@spec mission-substrate#approved-context) > all three Approved Context components (intent, proposal, derived authority_set) and their anchors survive successive state transitions unchanged

requirements.notes: The Approved Context is the Mission Intent, the recorded authority proposal where one was submitted, and the derived Authority Set ({{mission-architecture#oauth-statement}} item 4), not the Authority Set alone. The kernel's missions table (kernel.ts insertRecord) persists all three components (intent_json, proposed_authority_json, authority_set_json) and all three typed anchors (intent_hash, proposal_hash, authority_hash) together at creation; no UPDATE statement anywhere in kernel.ts ever touches any of those six columns (grep-verified: the only UPDATEs touch state/version/successor/grant_id/status_list_idx/containment_json/derivation_count/projected_from). The cited test approves a Mission WITH a submitted proposal (so all three components and all three anchors are actually present, not template-mode nulls), snapshots each by content, and re-verifies all six byte-for-byte across two successive transitions (suspend then resume) while state and version visibly advance.

requirements.text: After approval, the approved value MUST be immutable.

observation.normative: the approved value never changes after approval

tests.name: approved context commitment (@spec mission-substrate#approved-context) > all three Approved Context components (intent, proposal, derived authority_set) and their anchors survive successive state transitions unchanged

requirements.notes: Same kernel.ts persistence as maintain-or-commit above, for all three components: intent_json, proposed_authority_json, and authority_set_json (and their three anchors) are written once at insertRecord and never appear in any subsequent UPDATE statement; setState only ever writes state/version (and, for contain(), a separate containment_json overlay). The cited test transitions a Mission approved with a submitted proposal through two successive transitions and asserts all three components and all three anchors are unchanged by content (a snapshot comparison), not merely by reference.

requirements.text: Mutable operational fields, including current state and log entries, MUST be distinguishable from the approved value.

observation.normative: mutable operational fields (current state, log entries) are distinguishable from the immutable approved value

requirements.text: A binding MUST NOT silently replace the approved value behind an existing reference.

observation.normative: the approved value behind an existing reference is never silently replaced

requirements.text: Changing the Approved Context requires a new approval event and a new Mission Reference, unless a binding defines the change as approval of a new immutable version with its own unambiguous reference.

observation.normative: a changed Approved Context gets a new approval event and new Mission Reference, or an explicitly defined new immutable version with its own unambiguous reference

requirements.text: When a binding uses a commitment instead of retaining or disclosing the value, it MUST define:

observation.normative: the binding defines the exact committed bytes or canonicalization procedure, algorithm identification and agility behavior, domain separation sufficient to prevent cross-type substitution, and how a possessing party verifies the commitment

requirements.text: Every committed JSON value, and the envelope around it, MUST satisfy I-JSON

observation.normative: committed JSON values and their envelope satisfy I-JSON; non-conformant input destined for commitment is rejected before canonicalization: duplicate member names are refused at parse time before the parsed data model exists, string data is valid Unicode free of surrogate/noncharacter code points, and number data is representable as a finite IEEE 754 binary64 value

tests.name: parseStrictJson > rejects duplicate member names (core § canonicalization)

requirements.notes: Duplicate-member rejection is tested via the shared canonicalization primitive that substrate's Default Commitment Construction defines (#284 ruling); core.commitment.duplicate-members exercises the identical function under its own document tag. The I-JSON string (surrogate/noncharacter) and number (finite binary64) conformance arms have no test.

requirements.text: A verifier MUST reject a digest whose algorithm prefix it does not recognize and MUST NOT treat an unrecognized prefix as `sha-256`.

observation.normative: an unrecognized algorithm prefix is rejected outright and never silently compared as sha-256

tests.name: integrity anchors (core § test-vectors) > verifyAnchor round-trips and rejects unknown algorithm prefixes

requirements.notes: Same shared verifyAnchor primitive substrate's Default Commitment Construction defines (#284 ruling); core.commitment.unknown-prefix exercises the identical function under its own document tag.

requirements.text: a specification introducing a new prefix MUST define the carrier and schema of any parallel commitment, the binding that proves the old and new values commit to the same object, producer behavior during the transition, verifier selection and downgrade behavior when recognition sets differ, and the transition procedure itself.

observation.normative: a specification introducing a new digest-prefix algorithm defines the carrier and schema of any parallel commitment, the binding that proves the old and new values commit to the same object, producer behavior during the transition, verifier selection and downgrade behavior when recognition sets differ, and the transition procedure itself; no transition mechanism exists in this document, so an introducing specification carries the whole duty

requirements.text: A binding MUST define a native approval ceremony that atomically creates an active Mission Context or has equivalent transactional semantics.

observation.normative: the approval ceremony creates the active Mission Context atomically, or with equivalent transactional semantics: a failed creation leaves no partial record

tests.name: store baseline (D27) > transactions are atomic

requirements.notes: The shared store's transactional primitive (openStore/withTransaction over the missions table) is the generic mechanism substrate's approval ceremony requires; core's mission creation is built on it. This is a generic-infrastructure match rather than a @spec-tagged substrate test, recorded here for honesty.

requirements.text: The ceremony MUST:

observation.normative: the ceremony authenticates the Approver at the deployment's required assurance level, establishes the Actor per Actor Binding, presents or makes available a faithful representation of the approved context, records the approval decision/Approver/Actor binding/Approved Context or its commitment/Mission Reference/Controller, and initializes the Mission as active only after approval succeeds

requirements.text: the ceremony MUST NOT create the Mission Context without the Approver's consent to the changed context, and any commitment is computed over the context actually approved

observation.normative: a context change between presentation and decision blocks Mission creation absent the Approver's consent to the changed context, and any commitment covers the context actually approved

requirements.text: A binding MUST identify security-relevant material supplied by an untrusted proposer and describe how the approval ceremony prevents it from being mistaken for Controller-derived policy or trusted explanation.

observation.normative: the binding identifies untrusted-proposer-supplied security-relevant material and describes how the ceremony prevents it from being mistaken for Controller-derived policy or trusted explanation

requirements.text: Every binding MUST define an active predicate and a non-active outcome.

observation.normative: the binding defines an active predicate and a non-active outcome over its state vocabulary

tests.name: basic governance gate: state-gated issuance and derivation (@spec mission-substrate#basic-gate) > active predicate true -> gateActive and gateDerivation proceed
basic governance gate: state-gated issuance and derivation (@spec mission-substrate#basic-gate) > active predicate false -> gateActive and gateDerivation refuse, for every recognized non-active state

requirements.notes: The Controller is the Mission Issuer/AS ({{mission-architecture#oauth-statement}} item 2), not the resource-side PDP: the Basic Governance Gate is realized by src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/kernel.ts's gateActiveLineage, shared by gateActive (state-gated issuance/continuation) and gateDerivation (state-gated derivation, layering the max_derivations cap on top). The active predicate is `record.state === "active"` exactly; the non-active outcome is a thrown GateError, refusing both issuance and derivation. Both cited tests run unconditionally against the kernel's in-memory sqlite store, so this coverage never sandbox-skips. The PDP's evaluate.ts implements the analogous RESOURCE-side decision gate (a different Controller-vs-PDP role per the substrate's binding statement); its four basic-gate-shaped unit tests now back the runtime/authzen decision-request rows they genuinely prove (see runtime.decision-inputs.active-state-required and runtime.decision-inputs.authority-entry-and-subset-required and authzen.pdp-request.consistency-id-and-issuer-equal), not this Controller-role row.

requirements.text: The Controller MUST make a positive governance decision only while the Mission is active.

observation.normative: a positive governance decision is made only while the Mission is active

tests.name: basic governance gate: state-gated issuance and derivation (@spec mission-substrate#basic-gate) > active predicate false -> gateActive and gateDerivation refuse, for every recognized non-active state

requirements.notes: Same gateActiveLineage predicate as active-predicate-and-outcome above, on the Controller (AS kernel), not the resource-side PDP. The cited test sweeps every recognized non-active MissionState (`suspended`, and `terminated` with each of the reasons `revoked`, `expired`, `completed`, `superseded` and `parent_terminated`), persisting each directly on the record before asserting both gateActive and gateDerivation throw GateError, never a positive decision.

requirements.text: Every value or condition not recognized as active MUST fail closed for that decision.

observation.normative: any value or condition not recognized as active fails the decision closed

tests.name: basic governance gate: state-gated issuance and derivation (@spec mission-substrate#basic-gate) > a persisted state value outside the recognized lifecycle set fails closed, never treated as active

requirements.notes: This row's 'unrecognized' is a lifecycle value or condition, not an unknown action; an unmapped action is out_of_authority on the resource-side PDP, a different failure mode on a different actor (see runtime.decision-inputs.authority-entry-and-subset-required, which the PDP's unmapped-action test now backs instead). The cited kernel test writes a state string outside the MissionState set directly onto the persisted record (bypassing the type system, simulating a corrupted or future-versioned value) and asserts both gateActive and gateDerivation throw GateError with reason mission_not_active: the active predicate is a whitelist (state === "active"), so any unrecognized value fails closed by construction, never by an explicit blocklist entry that could omit a case.

requirements.text: The binding MUST define at least one authenticated means by which an authorized party can cause the Mission to become non-active.

observation.normative: the binding names an authenticated non-active-transition mechanism, identifies the authorized parties, and states the effect on subsequent Controller decisions

requirements.text: Authority derived from a Mission MUST NOT be usable indefinitely.

observation.normative: for every positive decision and every governed artifact, the binding states a reliance bound as either a maximum post-non-active residual interval or an artifact expiry bounded by/disclosed with the Approved Context; a decision or artifact with neither bound does not conform

tests.name: async-delegation terminal paths (@spec async-delegation) > absolute-lifetime clamp: the initial access token exp never exceeds the Mission expires_at

requirements.notes: core.tokens.exp-clamp tests the artifact-expiry-bound arm for core's issued credentials (exp capped by the Mission's expires_at). The decision-point residual-interval arm, and the general non-conformance-without-either-bound check, are untested at this generic level.

requirements.text: a stated bound SHOULD NOT exceed the interval the Mission's purpose requires

observation.normative: the stated reliance bound is no longer than the Mission's purpose requires

requirements.text: Each positive governance decision and each artifact that a binding claims is Mission-governed MUST carry, or be unambiguously joinable to, the Mission Reference and Controller namespace.

observation.normative: every governed decision or artifact carries, or is unambiguously joinable to, the Mission Reference and Controller namespace, and the binding defines the join and the party performing it

tests.name: M4 core enforcement tier > scenario 2: happy path -- in-authority read permitted, Decision Evidence recorded
M4 core enforcement tier > Decision Evidence carries the PDP emitter and the recomputable entry_digest

requirements.notes: Partial: the M4 enforcement tests thread the Mission Reference (mission_id) from the PDP request through the PEP decision to the retained Decision Evidence record, attributed to its emitter; a genuine cross-component chain (PDP, PEP, EvidenceStore). The underlying tests are tagged endpoint-level under their existing rows (runtime.evidence.decision-and-refusal-must-produce-record and others), so this row's cross-component level is not matched and it stays partial rather than tested. The Controller-namespace half is implicit (a single-issuer deployment), not a separately carried field, and this mapping does not exercise it.

requirements.text: Merely accepting an unverified reference supplied by the Actor does not establish Mission governance.

observation.normative: an unverified Actor-supplied reference, accepted without more, does not establish Mission governance

tests.name: basic gate: active predicate, non-active outcome, unrecognized-fails-closed > a supplied mission reference that mismatches the loaded view is refused, never silently accepted

requirements.notes: Partial: the cited unit-level test (unconditional, no live OpenFGA) proves a supplied context.mission.authority_hash that mismatches the independently loaded view is refused (view_inconsistent), never silently accepted. It does not prove the complementary half of this row's normative text, that an accepted reference must itself have arrived inside a verified credential rather than as a bare unauthenticated parameter; that is a token-binding/RS concern outside evaluate()'s pure-function boundary and untested here.

requirements.text: The binding MUST state what the propagation mechanism proves.  In particular, it MUST distinguish among:

observation.normative: the binding distinguishes correlation with a Mission Context, proof the Controller made a particular decision, proof a credential was issued under the Mission, and proof a requested operation is within approved structured authority; the kernel requires only the first, with authenticated or integrity-protected provenance

requirements.text: The Controller MUST maintain an integrity-protected, ordered record of governance events for the Mission.

observation.normative: the Controller maintains an integrity-protected, ordered governance-event record for the Mission

requirements.text: At minimum, the record MUST cover approval, positive and negative Controller decisions that rely on the Mission Context, and transition to a non-active outcome.

observation.normative: the record covers approval, positive and negative reliance decisions, and the non-active transition; events are attributable to their source and correlated with the Mission Reference

requirements.notes: The Controller MUST maintain this record ({{mission-architecture#oauth-statement}} item 9), not the resource-side PEP; mcp-payments's EvidenceStore records are PEP-side per-request decision evidence, not the Mission Record's approval evidence and lifecycle history, so they satisfy no arm of this row's minimum coverage (approval, positive/negative Controller decisions, and the non-active transition) and are not cited here. No Controller-owned record exists in src/ today: Mission Kernel approval and lifecycle-transition events (kernel.ts approve()/setState()) fan out only through the ephemeral onLifecycleCommit callback, never journaled into any persisted, queryable record. The mcp-payments decision-evidence tests remain cited, correctly, on the runtime-evidence Decision Evidence rows they do prove (the M4 enforcement-tier rows).

requirements.text: The binding MUST state its ordering semantics, integrity protection, authorized readers, and retention period.

observation.normative: the binding states the record's ordering semantics, integrity protection, authorized readers, and retention period

requirements.text: The retention period MUST include the active lifetime and a declared post-termination period.

observation.normative: the stated retention period spans the active lifetime plus a declared post-termination period

requirements.text: A binding MUST NOT claim a capability unless it meets every requirement in that capability's subsection.

observation.normative: a capability is claimed only when every requirement in its subsection is met

requirements.text: such scope is part of the claim and MUST appear in the Mission Substrate Statement

observation.normative: a capability's mode/role/operation/deployment scope is documented in the Mission Substrate Statement, not left implicit

requirements.text: Its Statement MUST enumerate those operations, such as authority derivation, delegation, credential issuance, credential refresh, permission decisions, or continued reliance.

observation.normative: the Statement enumerates the named authorization operations the Lifecycle-Gated Authorization claim covers

requirements.text: For every operation in the claim, the decision point MUST establish that the Mission is currently active before returning a positive result.

observation.normative: the decision point confirms current active state before returning a positive result, for every claimed operation

requirements.text: It MUST fail closed when current state cannot be established within the binding's stated freshness bound.

observation.normative: the decision point fails closed when current state cannot be established within the stated freshness bound

requirements.text: The binding MUST state the maximum interval during which a previously issued positive result can remain usable after the Mission becomes non-active.

observation.normative: the binding states the maximum post-non-active residual usability interval for a previously issued positive result

Over the MCP channel, one test signs three of these values side by side, each with no PDP call and no effect: request_invalid (the invalid_request diagnostic, arguments that fail an established action's served input schema, D334), request_unsupported (unknown_tool) and capability_source_unresolvable (a schema intake cannot read). target_unresolvable (the unknown_vendor diagnostic, #1251, D484): a lookup_vendor naming a vendor the store does not hold is refused with one verifiable signed Refusal Record carrying that value, no decision request and no Resource-policy query, under an unconstrained credential and under one that names the vendor, at the PEP over both decision channels and over the HTTP endpoint with DPoP; with D324's server fallback restored, the unconstrained lookup reaches the PDP and the named one signs credential_authority_insufficient, and each assertion fails. #786 enumerated the eight reasons this deployment previously emitted outside the set, so every emitted reason now maps to an enumerated value; #1148 (D379) makes the set a boundary the PEP cannot cross: its mapping is exhaustive over the Refusal Record path's diagnostics, an unmapped diagnostic rejects enforcement before anything is signed, and the evidence store refuses a value outside the emitting role's set. token_invalid, mission_claim_missing and mission_reference_conflict still have no assertion on a value the PEP signs, and remain #594 wave 4. requirements.notes: The Decision Evidence, Refusal Record and Execution Evidence `emitter` member definitions each restate this rule with an explicit in-text cross-reference back to this anchor; treated as duplicate-of-another-row rather than three additional rows. The vacuity the prior note recorded is closed (#741): the emitter id and audience are the deployment's real values (its canonical resource and the request audience) rather than the ephemeral signer's placeholders, the binding is enforced on the emission side too (an emitter refuses to sign for a scope its key does not serve), and a record whose emitter id or audience does not resolve is refused at retention with nothing retained. #594 W4-5 adds the configured key-set lookup: exact kid, emitter, role and audience for all three producer roles, with an absent or empty audience refused rather than wildcarded. Still partial: the keys are per-boot, in-process key material, not resolved through a published, deployment-scoped key set, because this deployment publishes no Enforcement Scope Statement instance carrying extensions.evidence.signing_key_locations. #853 (D487): key authorization comes from the declared Enforcement Scope Statement versions (enforcement_boundaries): the verifier resolves a key only when the record's (audience, kid) pair determines one authorization naming its emitter and role and one published key, a key authorized for one boundary never verifies a record for another, and the PEP's evidence store refuses to sign for a boundary its key is not authorized for. Still partial: the keys remain in-process key material, per boot by default; durable evidence key files (#831, opt-in) give the same material at every boot but do not change how a key is resolved. #853 review: each boundary publishes its keys at its own key-set location bound to it, so across a declared change a record verifies under its own boundary's set and never under the other's.

requirements.notes: #1868 (D999; fix/1868-producer-audience): the producer half of the audience member, beside the consumer row evidence.execution.audience-bound-at-settlement (D991), whose PDP witnesses establish nothing here. Role PEP covers the enforcement-side emitter: the suppression and the read completion are signed under the PEP role, the wire completion and the late record under the executor role of the same component. Applicability is unconditional with the runtime-enforced profile, as for the other PEP rows at this anchor: any enforcement point that emits Execution Evidence writes the member. Both identifiers of the witnesses' declared change are spelled with upper-case letters and a trailing slash (https://Payments.Example/Legacy/MCP/ replaced by https://Payments.Example/MCP/), so a normalized record differs from its Decision Evidence; a decision point that re-presents a held permit whatever version is in force stands in for a retransmission on the wire. The #853 in-flight witness asserts that the dispositions after the cutover of a read and of a compound action's prepare phase, both admitted before it, keep the old identifier. The idempotency-claim-pep reconciliation witness asserts only that one late record exists, not its audience, so it is not cited. Mutants at 695aa419, each alone with vitest in its own process group and the source restored byte-equal: the attempt taking the request's boundary (MA, the #1868 defect) fails the re-presented witness at the suppression record's audience; a lowercased (MB1) or trailing-slash-trimmed (MB2) copy fails it there too (no key is published for the normalized spelling, so no record is emitted) and fails the fresh-permit control's records; dropping the refusal of a retained record without an audience and falling back to the request's boundary (MC) fails the no-audience witness at its refusal, no-effect, no-record and Refusal Record assertions; the use check reading the copied audience and version instead of the boundary established now (MD) fails the re-presented witness at its refusal, ledger and redemption assertions (the old permit executes), and four existing #853 witnesses; the disposition record taking the boundary established at emission (ME) fails the re-presented and in-flight witnesses at the record's audience; the late record taking the emitter's configured identifier (ML1) or a lowercased copy (ML2) fails the late-record witness at its settlement and record assertions. Rerun with every assertion of the three new witnesses soft, each assertion of the producer's behavior fails on its own under at least one mutant; the seven precondition assertions (the permit issued, the identifier the linked Decision Evidence recorded, the redemption, no record before reconciliation, the record without an audience retained) hold before the producer acts and are killed by none.

requirements.notes: D991 (owner ruling on #1861): the consumer half of the audience member, a row of its own. These witnesses exercise the PDP's settlement intake and establish nothing about the PEP that writes the record; the producer duty needs its own witness at the PEP. Applicability: the duty binds whichever consumer settles a permit on Execution Evidence, the PDP's idempotency claim under the transaction-assurance tier (runtime#idempotency) or the metering settlement intake under exact budgets (metering#settlement-contract). The reference serves both from one claim domain, so the row applies under either capability (any_of), never under one mode alone. #1841 (D974; fix/1841-settlement-audience at c41a03f7, merged by #1861 at 4b4f5192): settle compares the authenticated record's audience byte for byte with the boundary retained for the permit's claim before any effect. Four other boundaries publish their own keys in one declaration (another port, the identifier with an upper-case host, the identifier with a trailing slash, the identifier truncated to its origin). Their records are refused audience_mismatch for completed, failed and suppressed outcomes on an unsettled claim, for a conflicting completed record, the applied attempt's suppressed record and a redelivery of the applied record's members after an applied failed settlement, and for a completed record after an incorrect operator release past the window. Each refusal leaves the claim row, its transitions, the conflict table, the reservations and both counters unchanged with no alert, the failed and suppressed records never reach the redemption owner, and the permit's own boundary's record settles in each case. The adoption witness settles a claim adopted across a declared identifier change at the adopting permit's boundary and refuses the replaced identifier's record; the legacy-file witness takes a pre-column row's boundary from its stored Decision Evidence and refuses boundary_unretained on a row without one. #1861's mutants at c41a03f7, each alone with the source restored: removing the comparison (M1) fails all seven at their refusal; moving it after the claim's settlement (M2) fails six, and after the late correction (M3) all seven, at the unchanged-state assertion alone; moving it after the redemption owner's query (M4) fails the failed and suppressed witnesses at the never-asked assertion; a case-insensitive (M5), record-prefix (M6), boundary-prefix (M7) or URL-normalized (M8) comparison fails the five boundary witnesses; treating a NULL boundary as a match (M9) or as the scope's audience (M10), dropping the backfill (M11) and letting a record with no claim row reach the correction (M12) fail the legacy-file witness; leaving the boundary unchanged at adoption (M13) or comparing the scope's audience (M14) fails the adoption witness; omitting the boundary at the claim (M15) fails six. Re-verified at main 4b4f5192 with the same runner: M1 fails 7 of 7, M2 six, M5 the five boundary witnesses and M13 the adoption witness, the source restored byte-equal after each.
