requirements.notes: #594 W4-8: retirement is anchored on the LAST artifact the key signed, not on its creation or its retirement instant, and the published document keeps the retired kid until that window elapses; a record signed before the rotation still verifies at the boundary and resolves key_not_resolvable one second past it. The retirement metadata is durable, so the anchor survives a restart; on the composed stack that holds with durable evidence key files (#831), whose key sets live in a durable file, and not with keys generated per boot, whose key sets the stack keeps in memory. The two composed-stack restart witnesses (D887) show the records an earlier boot signed verifying after a restart with durable evidence key files, and not with per-boot keys, and a regenerated key file refused at publication: what stays resolvable is retained, authorized public verification material, and nothing here retains a private key for verification. A rotation is a NEW kid: republishing a published kid over different material or a different binding is refused, since accepting it would strand every record that kid signed inside the window.

observation.local: the authority source is an injectable seam (AdapterOptions.authoritySource over kernel/derive.ts's EffectiveAuthoritySource); a source raising SourceUnavailableError maps to temporarily_unavailable/503 with Retry-After (provider.ts sourceUnavailableError plus the header middleware, continuation-grant.ts txError for the custom grants). The tests drive an injected failing source, which is the only way to reach the class here: the local kernel is the authoritative record and can be neither unreachable nor unverifiable to itself, and the rolled-back-version trigger has no external replica to roll back, so the discrimination BETWEEN the three triggers is the source's own duty and stays unobserved

requirements.notes: D361: its own store (kernel/dispatch-handoff-store.ts), not the DPoP replay cache: one INSERT on the jti primary key, no eviction of a consumed jti before exp plus skew. The store is in memory and built per boot like every AS store (D25/D27). The AS's signing keys can outlive a restart (a key ring, #831), so a restart cannot revive a consumed grant because each grant's jti names the process that issued it (a random boot identity, AdapterOptions.processBootId) and the AS refuses a grant another process issued: an unredeemed grant minted before the restart is refused too, a deliberate invalidation. An identity, not a start time: a restart within the second of issuance is refused as well (#1299 review P1, where a start-time floor accepted it). Persistent consumption records (#1163 review) would keep unredeemed grants redeemable across a restart and are #250's durable-store work. Witnessed with a key ring and a file-backed kernel, across a later second and within the same one, and proved by disabling the check and by sharing one boot identity across builds (the redeemed grant then redeems again). Taking is two-phase (#1163 review P2): the jti is reserved, confirmed once the token exists, and released when none is issued; the authority source is resolved before the jti is taken. requirements.notes: #813, D830; #1710, D877 item 4. One refusal witness per prohibited predicate, each committing nothing (impl/1710-prohibited-coverage at 3f72c8e1a). At /token a template whose ceiling is the whole derivation-policy ceiling (policy wide-reconciliation) dispatches a proposal of one action within both ceilings: payments:payment.execute (irreversible), payments:remittance.send (external commitment), payments:vendor.read (external communication), ledger:vendor.read or ledger:journal.write (cross-domain). Each case asserts that the published mapping gives the action exactly that predicate and that the shipped set lists it, then expects 400 dispatch_prohibited_class with no token and no mission_id, no new Mission, no dispatch event, and the same dispatch_event_id reusable for an admitted payments:invoice.read Dispatch. No shipped action is privileged administration, so that witness is at the kernel: a classification makes hr:role.grant privileged administration, the coverage check's gap adds it to the configured set, and the Dispatch is refused with no Mission and no dispatch event, while the shipped set, which leaves it out, admits it. The AAM e2e step 2 (live OpenFGA only) still witnesses remittance. Mutations (2026-10-26): a guard that refuses nothing fails the kernel gate test, the older /token test and every per-predicate witness; a guard that refuses only after the instance and dispatch event commit fails the five /token witnesses and the kernel privileged-administration witness; a guard that admits one listed action while the set still lists it fails that action's witness alone, for each of the six. The older /token test dispatches the whole wide ceiling, so it no longer isolates the irreversible class: admitting payment.execute leaves it passing while remittance and the vendor read still refuse. Slice 3a (impl/813-standing-payment-admission at a7063aab): under a designating template with the capability on, remittance and the payment where it is also cross-domain authority are refused dispatch_prohibited_class at /token, and the kernel refuses the payment where the mapping also classifies it privileged administration, external commitment or external communication. Mutations: the /token remittance test fails only when the predicate admission and the AGR high-risk gate are both disabled (two independent layers); the /token cross-domain test fails when the predicate admission refuses nothing, when every predicate of the payment is waived, or when the cross-domain predicate is unmapped; round-1 mutants kill the kernel tests.

The reference keeps the prohibition in the issuer's configured set, outside the policy snapshot, so the policy's own duty is witnessed through the issuer's refusal under a policy that would otherwise admit the instance. #1710 (impl/1710-prohibited-coverage at 3f72c8e1a): at /token a template under the wide-reconciliation Dispatch Policy (ceiling equal to the derivation-policy ceiling) is refused dispatch_prohibited_class, committing nothing, for one action per predicate the shipped set lists (payments:payment.execute, payments:remittance.send, payments:vendor.read, ledger:vendor.read, ledger:journal.write), and the same template, policy and dispatch_event_id then admit a payments:invoice.read Dispatch. requirements.notes: #813, D830; #1710, D877 item 4. The published mapping is configuration alone: config/approval-floor.json's classification (each action's class, and each classification's cross_domain statement: true for the ledger at http://localhost:4406/mcp, false for payments and reports) and config/progressive.json's external-communication actions (payments:vendor.read). approval-floor.json and enforcement-scope.json classify payments:payment.reverse as irreversible_action; the MUST is on the mapping, not on reachability. config/policy.json's dispatch_prohibited_actions lists payments:payment.execute, payments:payment.reverse, payments:remittance.send, payments:vendor.read, ledger:vendor.read and ledger:journal.write. #1710 (impl/1710-prohibited-coverage at 3f72c8e1a): a table test states the predicates the mapping gives each of the twelve served actions and that every classification states cross_domain; the shipped set is checked under all five predicates; one gap test per predicate shows the check names exactly that action under that predicate alone and throws (privileged administration has no shipped action, so its case adds a classification that makes hr:role.grant one); the AS's resource-to-AS map only adds cross-domain resources and never clears one the classification states. Mutations (2026-10-26): leaving payment.execute, remittance.send, vendor.read, ledger:vendor.read or ledger:journal.write out of policy.json fails the shipped-set test and the gap tests (payment.reverse: slice 3a, impl/813-standing-payment-admission at a7063aab); the ledger's cross_domain set false or removed, the mapping ignoring the statement or dropping the external-communication actions, or the predicate reader never adding cross_domain each fail the table test and the gap tests; a gap check that drops external communication fails the external-communication gap tests, and one that skips every classified action fails all five; a resource-to-AS map that no longer adds, or that overrides the classification, fails the cross-domain statement test. The check runs as a unit test, not a startup refusal: an AS whose resource-to-AS map places payments at another AS (the standing-payment /token cross-domain test) would see every payments read action as a gap.

observation.local: In the reference this is enforced before any Dispatch: with the standing-payment capability on, the AS refuses to start while it holds a designating Dispatch Policy whose budget omits any of owner, id, currency, limit or per_instance_max, rejecting construction with StandingPaymentConfigError 'Dispatch Policy <id>: standing_payment: budget is not {owner, id, currency, limit, per_instance_max}'. The missing-exception refusals are /token Dispatch refusals carrying dispatch_prohibited_class (M4-13, M4-13i, M4-reason, M4-36 above). The recency-ceiling clause is a startup refusal: the terms parser requires each exception to be exactly {max_age_s} with a positive integer, so a running AS holds no exception without a ceiling and no /token Dispatch can carry one, and the startup witness asserts StandingPaymentConfigError with the parser's message, never dispatch_prohibited_class. M4-ceil (kernel/standing-payment.ts `if (!isObject(exception) || !exactly(exception, ["max_age_s"]) || !positiveInteger(exception.max_age_s)) {` to `if (!isObject(exception)) {`) lets startup succeed, failing the startup witness at its rejects line. Re-verified on impl/813-as-rows-d974 at e3a3454df (source as main c841fd841), each mutant alone in its own process group, with the results above: M4-13, M4-13i, M4-reason and M4-36 at /token (M4-13 also against the kernel witnesses), and M4-ceil at startup. Dropping one branch of the check alone: exactly (MB-exactly) starts the AS for the extra member alone; positiveInteger (MB-positiveInteger) for the zero, negative, fractional, beyond-safe-integer and string ceilings; isObject (MB-isObject) still refuses every form, a null exception then refused with a TypeError message instead of the parser's, so that branch guards a crash the exactly branch otherwise covers. Slice 3b (impl/813-binding at 33a88d93): through the composed stack, an approved vendor's account changed between the permit and its use suppresses the permit at admission with target_drift, and nothing is wired. Reverification binds the payee twice, through the effective parameters parameter_digest covers and through the evaluation-context payee fact: freezing the fact (Rb) turns the refusal into parameter_mismatch and fails the witness, and blinding both layers (Rab) lets the wire execute; keeping the decided payee in the fresh parameters alone (Ra) survives by design, since the evaluation-context layer still suppresses. The approved vendor's account changes after the permit is decided on the committed account: the wire is refused target_drift, nothing is wired and the invoice stays payable, and the one suppressed Execution Evidence record carries the permit's parameter and context digests beside unequal effective ones. Freezing the payee fact the evaluation-context layer reads (R1: the payments-store:invoice.payee_account resolver returns a constant) turns the refusal into parameter_mismatch and fails it; blinding both layers (R2: R1 plus reverify's fresh parameters keeping the decided payee) wires the payment and fails it, and with the refusal assertion removed fails the nothing-wired assertion alone; blinding the parameter layer alone (R3) survives by design, since the context layer classifies first. Tested at endpoint; the cross-component citation stays. The no-release clause that follows is homed by metering.aggregate-bounds.fresh-consent-no-release. Slice 4 AS track (impl/813-as-slice4 at 03a9a4a6, D877): every designating template consent page, for the authenticated Approver, renders the shared budget's consumption to date (committed) and outstanding reservations (reserved, and held pending reconciliation) as read through the AS's budget exposure port; the render revision commits the figures, so a change before the decision refuses it (409 approval_context_changed); a reading that cannot be made, is deferred, or is not the counters' totals withholds the decision (503 page and 503 temporarily_unavailable decision, no template, proposal pending); an unauthenticated viewer sees no figures and no counter is read. Pre-enablement gap 1 (D947; impl/813-pre-enablement-as at 8f2d1558, mutation at the same commit): the exposure mutants re-run against the review-fixed code, each alone, all killed. O0 (startup port check removed) fails the port-required startup test. O1 (consent exposure lines not rendered) fails the rendering test at its exposure line, the render-to-decide test at its 409, the Approver half of the withholding test, the declared-exponent test, and the composed-stack consent test at its exposure line. O3 (consent figures left out of the commitment) fails the render-to-decide test at its 409. O7 (the stack port keys the shared counter by owner alone) fails the composed-stack consent test at its exposure line. O2 (consent read failure rendered as no exposure), re-targeted so the page and the decision go on without the figures, fails the read-failure page test at its 503 (page 200), the read-failure decision test at its 503 (409), and the three malformed-reading tests at their consent page's 503; its earlier text still applies but crashes the page render (500), so the re-targeted form is the one counted. Each mutant alone, all killed: dropping the consent exposure lines (O1) and dropping them from every Dispatch Policy version but 1 (D1, which no version-1 test kills) fail all three at the exposure line, the new terms having rendered; reading a counter per template_version (W1), per Dispatch Policy version (W2) or keyed by the Dispatch Policy id (W3) instead of the shared budget's fail all three at the exposure line; leaving the figures out of the commitment (O3) fails all three at the 409.

requirements.notes: #813, D830. The capability stays disabled and unclaimed. New at 9f8e8aca. Slice 3b (impl/813-binding at 33a88d93): the Mission Issuer's kernel derives each instance's budget binding (owner, id, currency, limit, committed policy, destinations and the instance's max_budget) from the Dispatch Policy snapshot the instance's activation retained, and the stack hands it to the co-resident decision point as its budget source. Taking the limit from per_instance_max (KB1) or dropping the destinations (KB2) fails the derivation witness; a stack source that answers nothing (Pa) or a kernel that derives no binding (Pb) lets the composed payment run unmetered and the changed-account payment execute, and Pb fails the end-to-end binding match. A snapshot that is gone or no longer reproduces the committed digest, an admission naming another policy or budget, a Mission without the instance's max_budget, a Child Mission anywhere in the lineage, or a missing predecessor or parent record derives underivable, never unbound: accepting them (F6 to F10, V9, V11; F10 and V10 by the reason assertion only) fails the kernel witness, and reading underivable, an unheld Mission or another issuer's Mission as unbound (F4, F5, F5b) fails the end-to-end one. That no Dispatch request value reaches the binding is observation.local (D877). Partial at that slice: no endpoint-level propagation witness (the binding reaches the runtime only through the kernel function and the composed stack). The end-to-end test was renamed by the owner review (the suppressed permit's reservation stays charged); the mutants named above ran against earlier forms of it whose asserted lines are unchanged. Slice 4 AS track (impl/813-as-slice4 at 03a9a4a6, D877): at /token a dispatch Intent carrying destinations or a budget is refused invalid_request as an unknown member, creating nothing, so no Dispatch request can supply either. Mutation: an Intent top level that is not closed (17) issues a token. D961 level review (impl/813-proof-as): unchanged. The AS has no HTTP surface for this conveyance: under decision d the binding is PDP-local, derived by the exported kernel function standingPaymentBudgetBindingOf, which the deployment wires as its decision point's budget source (demo/src/kernel-mission-view.ts); it is in no token, introspection response or req.context, so an endpoint-level witness would need a new AS surface. D974 ruling 3: level unit at surface propagation, the exported derivation being the AS's surface for the conveyance, with the composed-stack tests retained as the evidence of delivery to the runtime (Pa, Pb). Recorded kills: destinations (KB2), the limit (KB1), the digest binding and retained snapshot (F6 to F10, V9, V11), no Dispatch request value (17 at /token). Owner, budget identifier and currency (impl/813-as-rows-d974 at a3aa0ee58, source as main c841fd841), each mutant alone in its own process group, each failing the derivation witness's whole-binding equality on that member alone: MV-owner-id (`owner: terms.budget.owner` to `owner: terms.budget.id`) and MV-owner-ref (to `ref.id`); MV-id-owner (`budget_id: terms.budget.id` to `budget_id: terms.budget.owner`) and MV-id-ref (to `ref.id`); MV-cur-eur (`currency: terms.budget.currency` to `currency: "EUR"`), MV-cur-limit (to `terms.budget.limit`) and MV-cur-drop (to `undefined`). Each also fails the second-policy witness, which derives an instance under sp-binding-treasury (another owner, id, limit and payee): a member hardcoded to the first fixture's value survives the first witness and fails this one alone (MV-owner-lit 'payments-operator', MV-id-lit 'ap-standing-binding', MV-limit-lit '5000.00'). Equivalent, and surviving as expected: owner or id read from the admission's pinned identity (`root.budget.owner`, `root.budget.id`), which the derivation already requires to equal the policy's; and currency hardcoded to USD or read from the instance's max_budget, since the terms parser admits only a USD budget and the dispatch requires max_budget in the budget's currency. Tested: every clause is asserted and killed at the derivation, with delivery to the runtime at the composed stack.

requirements.notes: #813, D830. The capability stays disabled and unclaimed. Re-quoted against 9f8e8aca. Now a MUST in Metering's form (refused unless charged). Live: D830 ruling 3 refuses children; the charged-child alternative is deferred. Shares its witness with metering.capacity-across-missions.standing-consent-child-refused. Slice 3a (impl/813-standing-payment-admission at a7063aab): createChildMission under a standing-payment instance is refused delegation_not_permitted. Mutation: removing the child guard fails it (the refusal becomes not_strict_subset, since the proposal equals the parent's authority; a strict-subset proposal would show the guard alone refuses). Slice 4 AS track (impl/813-as-slice4 at 03a9a4a6, D877): at /token a Child Mission requested from a standing-payment instance, and from its expansion successor holding a children grant, is refused delegation_not_permitted and creates nothing. Mutation: removing the child guard (29) fails both only through the reason (not_strict_subset). D947 gap 2 (impl/813-child-refusal-witness at aa542b79): that child omitted delegation, so derivation gave it the policy ceiling's grant (max_depth 2, five children of depth 2), broader than the successor's (max_depth 1, two children of depth 1), and the strict-subset proof refused it with or without the guard. The new witnesses, at the kernel and at /token, send a child that restates the successor's per-payment bound, vendor and children grant, for a child actor the grant admits: under the successor, which carries the instance's max_budget, it is refused delegation_not_permitted (the kernel witness asserts the guard's own message), no grant is issued and nothing is created (Mission count and findChildren unchanged). Mutation, each run alone: mutant 29 (the guard line replaced by void 0) fails both by admission (the kernel creates the child; /token answers 200 with a child grant); mutant 29 with the refusal assertions removed fails the Mission-count assertions alone and, in a separate run, the findChildren assertions alone; the guard moved after the child's insertRecord fails the kernel witness's count (at /token the creation transaction rolls the child back, and that witness passes); a refusal with the same status and reason added at /token after the creation commit fails the endpoint witness's created() assertion. The existing witnesses pass unmutated. A kernel control, 'admits the same strict-subset Child Mission under an ordinary Mission holding the successor's Authority Set, outside any standing-payment lineage (#813)', creates the same child where the guard does not apply. On the dispatched instance itself no child is admissible without the guard either: the instance holds no delegation grant (a standing-payment ceiling admits none, refused at consent and re-checked at dispatch), so a derived child entry introduces the policy ceiling's grant (not_strict_subset) or lacks the children on-switch (delegation_not_permitted), and no single-layer mutant admits a child there; the instance witnesses prove ordering and reason. Partial: the observation names an instance holding authority admitted under the Standing Payment Exception. The guard's necessity is witnessed on the instance's expansion successor, which carries the budget forward but was not dispatched, so it is not an instance (template#instance-composition); on the dispatched instance the refusal also holds without the guard, as above. Whether this row's instance covers that successor is an owner ruling, open; until it is ruled the row stays partial. D877 ruling 1 keeps this refusal a tested prerequisite.

Shares witnesses with metering.capacity-across-missions.successor-continues-counter and metering.aggregate-bounds.standing-consent-successors-share. Slice 2 (#816, impl/816-budget-reservations 22c1fae0, decision point over a real claim-domain file): a successor bound to its predecessor's first Mission draws on the predecessor's instance counter and the same standing_consent counter with consumption to date; keying the instance counter by the successor's own id (T8f) fails it. Slice 3b (impl/813-budget-binding-3b at 62325958): through the composed stack an expansion successor's payment is metered on the dispatched instance's mission counter and the shared counter with consumption to date: refused quota_exceeded beyond the instance's remaining, then permitted to exhaust it, and no counter keyed by the successor exists. Deriving the successor unbound (U1) or keyed by its own id (U2) lets its payment run unmetered or on a fresh counter, and dropping the instance limit (Q3p) lets it through, each failing the witness. Slice 4 AS track (impl/813-as-slice4 at 03a9a4a6, D877): the AS-side prerequisite is witnessed but not cited here (role): at /token an expansion successor of a standing-payment instance, approved on its page, derives the same budget binding as the instance, rooted at it; a binding walk that stops at the Mission itself (30) fails it. D961 level review (impl/813-proof-runtime at 5a44a14e): the PDP's public surface is the decision request plus the budget source the deployment binds to its decision point (createDecisionPoint budgetBindings). The PDP never derives the successor chain; the Mission Issuer's kernel does, witnessed at the AS above and not cited here by role. So an endpoint witness at that surface can be built, and is: the successor witness of metering.capacity-across-missions.successor-continues-counter decides through createDecisionPoint, whose source answers the successor with the binding rooted at the dispatched instance while the caller's view carries a fresh one. The successor's payments reserve and commit on the predecessor's mission counter and the shared counter with consumption to date, are capped by the instance's max_budget, and no counter keyed by the successor exists. S2i (re-rooting at the successor's own id), S2ii (no instance cap), S2iii (the caller's binding metered) and S2iv (every binding dropped, so the successor would run unmetered) each fail it. Tested at endpoint.

observation.local: The reservation, the successor's insert (source ceiling against the committed root, effective expiry, retained policy snapshot), the carried derivation check and the predecessor's supersession run in one kernel transaction before the token is minted. A predecessor terminated between adjudication and the commit is refused at the commit with invalid_request and mission_expansion_status predecessor_state_changed, and a containment committed after adjudication fails the completion with authority_restricted_since_approval (Expansion reconciliation checks 1 and 3); neither creates, supersedes or reserves anything.

observation.local: Classes come from the deployment's actionClasses mapping (runtime action classes) and externalCommunicationActions; an unclassified widened action also falls back. The cross-domain arm (a widened resource whose authoritative AS, through resourceToAs, is not this issuer) falls back: a widening into the SaaS resource the RAS is authoritative for. The mapping cannot contradict the approval-authentication floor (#1255): the AS does not start when actionClasses maps an action the floor's classification (config/approval-floor.json) places, at any resource, in a class some floor applies to, to a class outside the fresh-approval set; an action the mapping leaves out falls back as unclassified. So no drawdown grants by policy alone an action the floor classifies high-risk.

requirements.notes: #1767 (D887). The reference Resource AS claims each grant's (issuer, `jti`) atomically before it mints the local token, and keeps the claim through the grant's `exp` plus a 300 s margin. Witnessed: a second presentation in one process; a base and a continuation ID-JAG replayed after a restart on the durable store, also with the issuer's clock ahead of the Resource AS's; concurrent presentations releasing one token; a grant never redeemed before a restart redeeming once after it; a missing or uninitialized store refused at boot; and each claim's retention and issuer scope. Mutation-proved: claims held only in memory fail the three restart witnesses and the store refusals; a check-then-claim split by an await fails the concurrency witness; a boot floor fails the never-redeemed witness, and a boot floor in place of the store also fails the clock-skew witness; accepting an uninitialized file, or creating a missing one, fails its refusal witness; keying on `jti` alone fails the scope witness; dropping the margin or the pruning fails the retention witness; a claim that always succeeds fails the in-process witness. D901: the owner reviewed these witnesses with #1776, and the composed stack carries the store: `pnpm as-native` requires `MISSION_RAS_REDEMPTIONS` whenever `MISSION_KEY_RING` is set and refuses a missing or uninitialized store before anything connects, creating none. Its composed witness redeems an ID-JAG under the ring's durable `as-continuation` key, restarts the target on the same files, and is refused the replay, while one never redeemed redeems once. Mutation-proved: the stack not giving the RAS its store fails the composed witness at the replay; a key ring not requiring the store, or the launcher not checking it early, fails the gate; shutdown not closing the store fails the second boot. A restored older copy of the store is not detected, a documented limitation (D901).

requirements.text: the effective authority is the intersection of the verified delegated `authorization_details`, the current entitlement of the mapped origin principal, and current resource and deployment policy. All three are required

observation.normative: both origin-principal-mapping entry points (Cross-Org grant adapter, ID-JAG RAS) consult the mapped local principal's current entitlement unconditionally on every redemption (RAS: base AND continuation grants alike) via the shared EntitlementResolver contract, independently of the static authority-ceiling intersection and of the mapping's own validity bound; a missing, negative, stale-beyond-bound, future-dated, or resolver-exception result each refuse the same way as the other dual-axis failures, and never proceeds as entitled. The observation carries two grains. A bare Boolean is audience-scoped: it authorizes the complete already-intersected authorization_details set for that audience, unmodified. An observation carrying the OPTIONAL authority member is action- and resource-scoped: all three consumers (Cross-Org grant adapter, ID-JAG RAS, PDP) intersect the delegated set with it on exact (resource, action) matching, mint or evaluate the surviving subset when the match is partial, and refuse with the existing non-oracular error only when the intersection is empty, so the quoted text's per-entry intersection is exercised, not only its audience-wide instance. RAS minting additionally intersects the result per action with its REQUIRED configured ceiling, preserves constraints and retained-action provenance, and refuses an empty result before consuming the grant. requirements.notes: D858. RFC 3339 Section 5.7 permits an actual leap second, so this is a normative restriction, not a clarification; it covers the Common Constraints Resource Access defines and does not extend to companion-defined ones (D865). A client generating a proposal is bound too; the authorization server's refusal of one is resource-access.entry-validation.date-time-leap-second-refused. The reference enforced it before the rule through its shared parser. Proved by mutation: a parser admitting :60 fails both witnesses. An actual leap second on the last day of a year is still refused under that mutation by the calendar roll-over check, so the offset form and the :60 at no leap second carry the proof. requirements.notes: #1756 slice B3 (D902). The leaf's tools and mission_constraints become the presented credential's authority, which the PEP's existing credential bound enforces against the facts it establishes from its own records (the invoice's vendor and amount; the arguments carry only the invoice identifier). A presentation the substrate permits for a 125 USD invoice under a USD 100 leaf is refused out_of_authority before any decision, with a credential_authority_insufficient Refusal Record, over the in-memory channel; an invoice whose amount passes the cap after validation is refused before the decision, and one that changes between decision and execution is refused parameter_mismatch with no effect. Proved by mutation: dropping the leaf's constraints from the credential authority, and reading the root's authority instead of the leaf's, each fail a witness. D932 (owner review of #1792): the value enforced is the invoked tool's alone. The proof names the tool (aat_tool); its own mission_constraints names the contract the operation is performed under, whose Operation Profile must establish that tool's target; and the credential authority is that tool's entry alone, bound to the one invocation (tool name and arguments) it was verified for. Before the fix every leaf tool's authority reached the PEP, which could select another tool's retained contract: a presentation verified for a wildcard service tool executed under an invoice-level retained contract whose tool admitted only another invoice. Witnessed: that substitution is refused out_of_authority before any decision; a presentation naming the retained-contract tool executes under that contract; a tool whose own contract establishes another target is refused with a Refusal Record; and facts used for another tool or other arguments are refused at intake. The leaf's resource_contract is enforced end to end (D932 ruling 6): absent where the resource requires one it is refused before any decision, one the resource does not declare is refused at verification, and one withdrawn between the decision and the release suppresses the effect. Proved by mutation: passing every leaf tool's authority, computing the tool under the live profile, dropping the tool-to-contract binding, dropping the intake binding, ignoring the invoked tool in the Mission layer, not requiring a required contract, and not re-resolving the contract at use, each fail a witness. The row level is cross-component (B1 had placed unit on the blocked row): each witness mints at the AS kernel, verifies at the payments server and enforces at the PEP.

requirements.notes: #249 implementation (D553, payments-runtime-profile-v13). Where configuration requires a reference for any operation of the entry's resource (#1847, D989: the approval rule is per resource, enforcement per operation), the rendered set (kernel.derive), the approved record and the issued token carry the current reference; where it does not, none is attached. Enforcement is optional as shipped: the declaration requires no reference, so the endpoint witness configures one that does; mandatory adoption and the migration of unpinned approvals are separate (#249). Proved by not recording it. Template consent (#249 B.1, D875) is a new approval: the proposal, the consent page and the commit assemble the ceiling's references, the commit of the service-token stand-in and of the boot seed (no page) assembles at the commit only, and the template commits exactly the rendered ceiling. Proved by mutation, each alone: the proposal, the page, the decision's commit, the stand-in's commit, or createTemplate not assembling fails a witness. Governed adjudication (#249 B.2, D875) is a new approval: the bounded set is assembled before any rule or model evaluates it, so the preview, the committed Authority Set and the re-check carry the same reference. Proved by mutation: removing the assembly fails the witness. An Expansion (#249 B.3, D875) is a new approval: successorAuthority, which its page, decision, completion check and createExpansion share, assembles the successor's references. Proved by mutation: removing that assembly fails the witnesses. A progressive ceiling consent (#249 B.4, D875) is a new approval: the offer is assembled before the authorization page and an Expansion's review render it, and the consent commits the assembled ceiling. Proved by mutation, each alone: the page's offer, the review's offer or assembledCeilingOffer not assembling, or a consent commit not handed the declarations, fails a witness. #1847 (D989): with only the execute required, a read-only entry and a mixed read and write entry record the current reference, at the kernel and through /token, and an uncovered or doubly covered entry is refused with no Mission. Proved by mutation, each alone: deciding the requirement per listed action fails the read-only witnesses; approving an uncovered entry without a reference, or taking the first of two current contracts, fails the refusal witness.

requirements.notes: #1751, D875. Child delegation derives under the policy ceiling, which carries no reference; inheritResourceContract carries the reference of the one parent entry that with it authorizes the whole child entry, never borrowing, combining or choosing, and the inherited reference is checked as a carried one (a retired version refuses the child). Proved by mutation, each alone: no inheritance, choosing among disagreeing covering entries, borrowing from any entry for the resource, replacing a proposed reference, and skipping the carried-reference check each fail a witness. Partial until the other derivation paths are witnessed. Template Dispatch (#249 B.1, D875) is preservation-only: the instance carries the template ceiling's reference without the Dispatcher restating it, a Dispatcher reference the ceiling lacks is refused out_of_template_ceiling, and the instance's references are checked as carried ones. Proved by mutation: comparing the policy-derived half with references, failing the invariant instead of refusing, or skipping the carried check each fails a witness. Governed activation (#249 B.2, D875) preserves a pinned root ceiling's reference and refuses a proposal naming another; against an unpinned root the assembled entry is compared without its reference. Proved by mutation: comparing the policy-derived half with references, or an unpinned root exactly, fails a witness. A ceiling drawdown (#249 B.4, D875) is preservation-only: every wire drawdown check (the non-widening check, the encounter facts and the decision) decides on drawdownRequested's set, and the creation inherits onto the derivation before capability bindings are added, both carrying the consented ceiling's reference through inheritResourceContract, never one assembled afresh, and checking it as a carried one. Two endpoint witnesses draw down through /token: under unchanged configuration, and with the consented version superseded within its retention and no current version. Proved by mutation, each alone: inheriting after capability bindings are added fails both endpoint witnesses; deciding the non-widening check, or every wire check, on the assembled derivation fails the superseded one; and not inheriting in either place, or skipping the carried check, fails a witness.

requirements.notes: #1266 round 2 (D480 departures closed). An entry approved for another audience is not carried in this token at all (#1503 finding 7, D733); it is checked when a token is issued for its own resource (the boundary case). The cross-domain ID-JAG goes to the RAS, not to the resource server: the RAS's destination policy governs emission to the destination resource and is now fail-closed. Introspection discloses what was minted and emits nothing new. A scope-only target stays governed by the scope projection's independently enforced controls. The shipped mapping vouches exactly what each resource's metadata advertises (payments, SaaS). Mutations: dropping the AS refusal, checking every carried entry regardless of audience, letting an absent list pass, disabling the transaction-token check, loosening the mapping parser, the RAS passing an unlisted resource, the RAS passing an empty list, and the RAS stripping the key instead of dropping the entry each fail these tests. Review on PR #1427 (P2): the pairing was by equality, so an invoice-level or prefix entry under an audience skipped its list. Fixed with the overlap pairing over #1434's matcher. Mutations: pairing by equality only, checking only the first overlapping audience, a raw string prefix in place of prefixAdmits, dropping the prefix-contains clause, the RAS accepting any one overlapping list, and the RAS passing an entry that overlaps no listed resource each fail these tests. The transaction token admits only entries naming the Challenge-Issuing Resource exactly, so only the equality pairing is reachable there; the two-audience case is witnessed at the shared check.

requirements.notes: #1258 item 4; refusal approved in the #1277 review (D454), shape ruled in D457; implemented by #1278. One presence check (refusedEntryMember in @mission/core) backs every boundary: the published schema carries "locations": false (its top level closed to the supported set by #1399), validateMissionResourceAccessSchema covers PAR, device submission and the other proposal intakes, and the deferred, handoff and async-delegation exchanges check requested entries before projecting them. The RAS's intake, a different surface from PAR, applies the same presence rule to a carried entry through isAuthorityEntry, since its trusted issuers are configurable (the #1283 review): a trusted issuer's signed grant whose entry carries locations is refused invalid_grant, the RFC 7523 grant-level error rather than invalid_authorization_details, minting no local token, so SaaS never receives it (mapping-entitlement.test.ts, and cross-domain.test.ts end to end). The helper-level witness (authority-subset.test.ts: isAuthorityEntry and both narrowToCeiling operands) and the RAS local ceiling's startup refusal are not cited; a grant without locations, or carrying capability_sources, still mints. observation.local: the reference checks letter-digit-hyphen labels of 1 to 63 octets and 253 octets overall and, for an xn-- label read in lower case, the structural checks: it decodes under Punycode (RFC 3492) and encodes back to itself (RFC 5891 Section 5.3), and the decoded form holds a non-ASCII character, is in NFC and lower case as decoded, does not begin with a combining mark (Section 4.2.3.2), and meets the hyphen restrictions (Section 4.2.3.1). It does not check the RFC 5892 code-point classes (RFC 5891 Section 4.2.2), the contextual rules (CONTEXTJ and CONTEXTO, Section 4.2.3.3) or the Bidi rule (Section 4.2.3.4, RFC 5893), so a label only those refuse, such as xn--n3h (U+2603, DISALLOWED), is admitted

requirements.notes: #1376 states the rule. D858 accepts structural A-label checks as partial implementation coverage, and D865 keeps the row partial: structural checks and agreement between two consumers do not establish full IDNA2008 validity. Exercised at PAR: a non-ASCII label, an empty label, a trailing dot, and an xn-- label that does not decode or decodes to a form not in lower case, not in NFC, beginning with a combining mark, beginning with a hyphen, or with hyphens in its third and fourth positions; an A-label is accepted in any ASCII letter case (resource-access.entry-validation.recipient-domain-case). Not checked, hence partial: the RFC 5892 code-point classes, the contextual rules and the Bidi rule (observation.local). Proved by mutation, each alone: stripping a trailing dot before the label check admits example.com.; a label pattern admitting any non-dot character admits exämple.com; removing the NFC, lower-case, leading-combining-mark, leading-or-trailing-hyphen or third-and-fourth-hyphen check admits its case at PAR; and a recipient_domain syntax without the A-label checks admits them all. The round-trip check, which RFC 5891 Section 5.3 requires explicitly, has no witness found in 500,000 random inputs: none decoded but failed to encode back to itself. It is kept. The decoder never throws (unit witnesses for a truncated integer, an overflow, a code point past U+10FFFF and a surrogate). Cases ev-rd-01, ev-rd-02 and ev-rd-04 to ev-rd-10 run (entry-validation); ev-rd-03 and ev-rd-11 are valid controls. The second consumer checks the same structural subset.

A

requirements.text:
A verifier MUST reject an instance failing any of these checks,
treating the failure identically to a signature or schema failure

observation.normative: a well-formed, correctly signed, schema-conformant instance naming a Mission or producer role the signer is not authorized for is rejected as not verified, the same as a signature or schema failure

requirements.text:
This duty
falls on the producer at the moment of emission; the producer
discharges it either by retaining the instance itself, or by
delivering it to an evidence store or collector the deployment
designates for this purpose, whose successful acknowledgment of
receipt discharges the producer's own retention obligation.

observation.normative: the retention obligation for a Mission Evidence Envelope instance falls on the producer, discharged either by the producer's own retention or by successfully acknowledged delivery to a designated collector

observation.normative: an Intent Submission Evidence entry of type mission-intent-admission-assertion carries exactly type and assertion, nothing else

whose `alg` is `none`, whose `alg` does not match the algorithm family
of the key `kid` resolves to, or whose protected `typ` is not exactly

requirements.text:
the AS MUST use an atomic
   compare-and-set (or equivalent single-writer-wins primitive)
   against a store keyed by (admission issuer, `jti`), succeeding only
   if no prior submission has reserved or committed that key within
   its validity window.

observation.normative: jti reservation is an atomic compare-and-set keyed by (admission issuer, jti); a concurrent submission that loses the race is refused as replay and never verified in parallel

requirements.text:
On success, **commit** the
    `jti` reservation of step 7 (permanent, see above). On failure at
    this step or any of steps 2-9, **release** the reservation.

observation.normative: a jti reservation is committed permanently only on full verification success; any failure releases the reservation so a legitimate retry can reuse the identifier before expiry

requirements.text: Reusing the issuance profile's commitment mechanisms supplies canonicalization and algorithm identification and agility. It supplies nothing else

observation.normative: The Default Commitment Construction reused by this profile supplies only canonicalization (JCS, I-JSON) and algorithm identification/agility (the sha-256: prefix and reject-unknown-prefix rule); it supplies no authenticity, approval-time-existence, or selective-disclosure property.

requirements.text: The commitment is an unkeyed digest over Mission Record fields held under the same trust as the record itself. An issuer that can rewrite the record can recompute a matching commitment; authentication comes entirely from the signature of whichever artifact discloses the commitment, never from the digest construction

observation.normative: A bare approval_context_commitment proves nothing an attacker who controls the Mission Record cannot reproduce; whatever authenticates a disclosed commitment is the signature of the artifact carrying it (a Consent Evidence object, an Approval Governance Record, or a future Mandate claim), never the digest itself.

requirements.text: A matching commitment shows the disclosed facts are internally consistent with the retained record. It does not show the facts were true, or that an approval occurred, at the time claimed

observation.normative: A verifier that confirms a matching approval_context_commitment has confirmed internal consistency with the retained record only, never that the recorded approval genuinely occurred at the claimed instant.

requirements.text: The commitment is a flat digest over the complete manifest object; proving anything about one member requires disclosing the whole object

observation.normative: There is no mechanism to prove one manifest member (for example, subject) without disclosing every other member of the same manifest.

requirements.text: `approval_context_commitment` MAY appear as a signed member of an artifact that already authenticates a reference to the Mission

observation.normative: A companion artifact that already authenticates a reference to the Mission (for example, a Consent Evidence object) may add approval_context_commitment as an OPTIONAL signed member, and an introspection response may disclose it to a caller holding the existing member-scoped disclosure privilege that already gates proposal_hash.

requirements.text: A Relying Auditor re-checks an evaluation by replaying it from retained evidence

observation.normative: a re-check verifies the record; recomputes approval_policy.digest over the retained snapshot and, where that snapshot commits a separate evaluator that decides, the evaluator's activation policy reference digest; obtains the recorded inputs, including each model output in full, bound to the record's approval_event_id, the Mission's intent_hash and the authority_hash of the set recorded as evaluated, with each contributing service assertion matching one; re-runs the deciding policy or evaluator over them, approving with exactly the contributing set; and re-applies recency at evaluated_at. Missing evidence, a digest mismatch, a failed binding or a different replayed outcome leaves the evaluation not re-checked
observation.local: Witnessed on committed governed_policy records, the one basis under which the reference commits a record and retains the deciding policy's inputs: recheckApprovalGovernanceRecord, a reference Relying Auditor reading the issuer's retained store, replays each step, counting what the deciding policy counts rather than what the record lists, and each step's refusal is witnessed alone, including missing root, evaluator and input evidence and a high-risk class's recency exception. Recorded direct approvals re-check too (#1470 slice 1): the retained rule snapshot reproduces approval_policy.digest; no separate evaluator decides; the retained inputs are bound to the event and Intent, name the Mission's Approver and Subject, the authority source its retained binding names and the ceiling it consented, and record a well-formed authentication; the rule replays at evaluated_at over them with the human assertion equal to the recorded authentication, the committed Authority Set and exactly the human assertion contributing; policy-approval recency does not apply to it. Standing-consent bases other than governed_policy commit no record, so are not re-checked. Recorded ceiling drawdowns re-check too (#1470 slice 2), from retained state alone: the recording rule's snapshot reproduces approval_policy.digest; the deciding drawdown policy's retained snapshot verifies and parses to the recorded rules; the inputs are bound to the event, Intent and Authority Set, to the predecessor as committed (its own ceiling, narrowed or not, separately from the consented one; an effective set within its Authority Set, which a contained predecessor's narrowed set satisfies; its chain's drawdown instants), and the consent provenance to the consenting ancestor's own record; the drawdown decision replays to a policy activation over the retained inputs (children, restrictions, rate history, classes, cross-domain, instant), the record passes the commit gate, and the eligibility gate and recency replay at evaluated_at. For every basis, step 1 binds evaluation.evaluated_at to the Mission's creation, the atomic-commitment instant, so a re-signed evaluation instant is refused and each replay and recency check runs at the actual decision time; the replays' own refusals are witnessed on faulty-issuer records whose Mission commits at the moved instant. The drawdown replay's other inputs (live children, restrictions, external-communication actions, cross-domain, the rate bound) have no committed counterpart and replay as retained; the gate replays the committed rule's classification, which covers the decision's class check.

requirements.notes: #1436 item 12: defines the re-check that Conformance's Relying Auditor MUST already names, as present-tense steps with no new keyword. On owner review of #1452 at f8f5e6ec (P2): the re-check also retrieves and verifies the deciding evaluator and the recorded inputs, since a narrowing model output's service assertion carries only identifiers; missing evidence leaves the evaluation not re-checked. #1313 follow-up: tested by the reference re-check auditor. On owner review of #1471 at cebf665b (two P2s, D597): the counted set came from the record's own assertions, so removing assertions with their contributing entries re-checked (skipping recency when all were removed), and the event and Intent bindings held only per model output. The replay now counts the accountable policy assertion plus one service assertion per consulted model output, and the inputs as a whole carry the event and Intent; the regression cases fail on cebf665b. Mutations: each of 21 checks at the time (record verification, root snapshot presence and digest, evaluator identity and snapshot, root-decided deciding digest, input presence, the set-level event and Intent bindings, each model output's event, Intent and evaluated-set bindings, service-assertion matching, approval, Authority Set, the governed record gate, one service assertion per model output, contributing, recency order, age and class exception) disabled alone fails a witness. #1470 slice 1: the direct replay; each of its checks disabled alone fails a witness. On owner review of #1484 at 41a1f750 (three P2s): the direct replay bound neither the consented ceiling nor the source root to the Mission; a malformed evaluated_at made the floor's age comparisons false; and the rule parser accepted an unknown action class, disabling a floor. Fixed: step 4 binds the inputs to the Mission's retained source binding and consented ceiling and refuses a malformed recorded authentication, step 5 refuses an evaluated_at that is not an RFC 3339 timestamp (as does the evaluator), and the rule's floor passes the approval-floor policy's strict validation. Each regression case fails on 41a1f750. #1470 slice 2 (D626): ceiling_drawdown records; the consent walk is witnessed through a narrowed chain. On owner review of #1522 at 58f9ede1 (two P2s): the drawdown replay took the predecessor's ceiling from the inputs alone, so a narrowed predecessor's replay ceiling replaced by the original consented one re-checked; and the signed assertion, the evaluation and both replay instants could agree on a backdated instant. Fixed: step 4 binds the replay to the predecessor as committed (its ceiling, an effective set within its Authority Set, and its chain's drawdown instants), and step 1 binds evaluated_at to the Mission's creation for every basis, which also closes the same backdating in the direct and governed re-checks and subsumes the RFC 3339 check on evaluated_at. Each regression case fails on 58f9ede1. Mutations: 58, one per check across the consent walk, the gate, the record gate, every re-check step (including the creation-instant and predecessor bindings), the commit and the adapter, all caught; rerun with the creation-instant binding, the governed re-check's 22 all caught, and the direct record's 52 all caught but the commit's own gate call, unreachable as in slice 1; the direct replay-instant mutant became equivalent and was dropped.

requirements.notes: Two halves in one transaction: a per-row conditional UPDATE (`changes === 1`) binds the scalar committed inputs, and a descendant-set membership pass compares the whole current subtree against the manifest, which per-row CAS cannot do. Witnessed separately: a counter-only mutation with no version bump, a fan-out occupancy change, the termination of a rendered row, and a descendant created after approval. Under all-or-nothing each refuses the whole completion; under disclosed exclusions only a committed change class excludes and an uncommitted one still refuses. #919 adds a suspension and a resume after rendering, containment after approval, a rendered record gone at completion, and a discharge after rendering. Containment and discharge are compared by the membership pass: the committed `containment_version`, the committed `discharged_digests` as a set (#1673, D803) and `effective_authority_hash`; the conditional UPDATE binds the scalar inputs only. A latch on an entry containment already removed leaves the effective authority unchanged, so under a plan excluding only state changes only the discharge-set comparison refuses it; disabling that comparison fails its witness alone. Proved by mutation: disabling the membership pass and the UPDATE check together fails the suspension, resume, record and state-only discharge witnesses; dropping only the `record_missing` divergence fails the record witness; dropping only the effective-authority comparison fails the state-only discharge witness, where the plan excludes the discharge's state change but not its narrowed authority. With both halves off, the containment and all-or-nothing discharge witnesses are still refused by another check, so they are not the halves' discriminating witnesses. #1674: a carried row is compared as observed through the expiry clock, so an old child whose own expiry arrived before completion diverges as `state_changed` though no transition was persisted: refused under all-or-nothing, excluded and recorded `expired` under a plan committing that class. A cascade row is compared as stored, since its outcome does not change. Proved by mutation: comparing carried rows as stored fails the exclusion witness; comparing every row as observed fails the rendered-cascade own-expiry witness. #1675: a missing rendered row excluded under a plan committing `record_missing` must still be recorded; without a usable tombstone the completion is refused.

requirements.notes: Successor activation, every replacement record, every external transfer, the required old-child cascades, the complete final map, the authenticated Carryover Evidence, the terminal tombstones and the durable outbox payloads commit in ONE transaction. A mid-batch failure after a replacement already existed leaves no successor, no replacement, no cascade and no published event. The completion asserts that no descendant is left non-terminal, so the post-supersession cascade is a genuine no-op and nothing transitions outside the committed map. A crash between commit and publication redelivers each carried transition byte-identically from the durable outbox over a file-backed store, and the retained map and signed evidence are read back rather than recomputed.

observation.local: the reference AS authorizes only the parent's own client_id (an actor_token is carried, never used to authorize another client, #433) and answers invalid_request with no Mission state. The check precedes the lookup, so another client's retained completed operation is refused rather than recovered. A child another client created before the check could still derive credentials: its grant redeems, and a refresh family opened from it outlives the grant. So building the AS revokes every non-terminal child whose retained creation operation names a client other than its parent's (revokeChildrenCreatedByAnotherClient), and issuance gating then refuses the grant and every credential derived from it. The child record names no creating client, so a child whose creation operation was purged before the fix cannot be identified (#1326). Partial: the actor_token arm is not exercised.

requirements.notes: #1303, #1503. Proved by mutation: projecting a request with neither the subset check nor the issued-whole check fails the excess, relaxation and narrower-family witnesses (removing the subset check alone is masked by the issued-whole check, which also refuses those requests); deciding it only after consumption fails the before-rotation witnesses; the raw grant rar as the ceiling fails the contained witness; the Mission's effective set as the ceiling, ignoring the presented grant, fails only the narrower-family witness; returning the ceiling from the code-exchange hook fails the code witnesses. The async-delegation exchange's Mission check is witnessed by a request its presented handle still carries after containment; disabling that check fails the witness. #1513: the async-delegation exchange also refuses a request its projection cannot issue whole, such as an entry naming a capability_sources binding the Mission does not record (beyond the grant under the Subset Rule), which it had opened as a narrower family; the check compares each requested entry with its own projection, so a sibling entry for the same action cannot cover a dropped one; disabling it fails the two #1513 witnesses alone, and comparing the whole set instead fails only the overlap witness, and the whole-issue refusal carries its own description, so the containment witness still catches the Mission check alone. #1720 item 3 (D859): the AROP deferral initiation answered an excess invalid_request; it answers invalid_authorization_details, apart from the not-active, ownership and authentication refusals, which keep their codes. Mutation-proved: answering the initiation's subset failure invalid_request fails the AROP witness; removing the initiation's subset check fails it, the request then pending. #1740 (D862) then answers the Mission's own client invalid_grant for a Mission that is not active; the ownership and authentication refusals keep their codes.

Witnessed on every mint path that can meet an entry approved for another audience: the code exchange, the refresh, the device redemption, the Deferred Mission Approval, template dispatch, Expansion completion, the delegated Token Exchange (an Expansion successor holding an entry approved before the requested audience was mapped), the child JWT-bearer redemption (a Child Mission whose entries are approved for different audiences), and the async delegation family (refused before any side effect). Each path's own filter is told apart from the save-time check: without it the token is refused rather than issued narrowed.

requirements.notes: #1399 (D538). One shared set (SUPPORTED_ENTRY_MEMBERS and unsupportedEntryMember in @mission/core, beside REFUSED_ENTRY_MEMBERS) backs every boundary that admits or rebuilds a mission_resource_access entry: the published schema (top level closed), the proposal validator and the requested-authority intakes (refusedMemberViolation), direct derivation, template consent, the config loaders, isAuthorityEntry (foreign grants), projection and isSubsetEntry. The ceiling side of an exchange that issues requested entries unprojected (the ICA continuation, the deferral initiation) rests on isSubsetEntry: a comparison involving an unsupported member is refused unless the two entries are byte-identical under the canonical form, which keeps the Subset Rule's equal-entry clause, since an identical candidate carries the member unchanged. The approved set is rebuilt member by member, so no intake produces that state; the ceiling witnesses write it into the stored record. The ICA witnesses and the stored-record helper are ported from a parallel build of #1399 (68d7d7b7). Proved by disabling each guard alone, each caught only by its own witnesses: the request-side validator branch (the PAR, device, refresh, deferral, handoff, async and ICA candidate tests fail; with it disabled the handoff and async exchanges are still refused by projection's drop, on the subset message, so those two catch it by the message), derivation's check (the three derivation tests), each projection guard (one test each), isAuthorityEntry (the RAS test and the mission-core helper tests), template consent, the config loader check, the closed schema, the capability_sources type check, and the isSubsetEntry guard (the ICA ceiling witness, the deferral initiation's ceiling witness and the helper test). The deferral initiation answers that ceiling case invalid_authorization_details (#1720 item 3, D859), so its witness is cited; re-proved after the remap: ignoring the reference side's unsupported member in isSubsetEntry fails it alone in dtr-endpoint.test.ts. Not cited, since their error or level differs from this row: the config loaders (a native configuration error naming the entry and the member) and the template admin plane (invalid_request), witnessed in unknown-entry-member.test.ts and template-dispatch-endpoint.test.ts. Positive controls: resource_match exact and capability_sources are still admitted and derived, and the same requests without the member are issued. Resource Access's entry-validation list names no top-level-member rule, so the row quotes the OAuth binding's Subset Rule posture. No vector case.

observation.local: the reference authorization server acting as the MAS (services/authorization-server/src/adapters/join-assertion.ts, kernel/join-evidence-store.ts) and the MAS pilot (demo/src/mas-pilot/mas-as.ts): each minting writes its event (mission issuer and id, token sha256 and its one confirmation, join, caller, audience, mapping_version, iat, exp) to the kernel database after the last Mission re-read and before the assertion is cached or returned; a write that fails answers unavailable (503) with nothing returned or cached, so a retry mints anew. Each event is kept until a retain_until written when it is recorded: its Mission's expires_at plus the kernel's declared audit retention, the one value its terminal tombstones and activation policy snapshots compose. The pilot's MAS declares the deployment's audit horizon, AUDIT_HORIZON_SECONDS (config/policy.json audit_horizon_s, 31536000 seconds: one year after Mission expiry, D770); the reusable kernel's default (7776000 seconds) applies only where a deployment declares none. Boot recovery deletes only events whose stored retain_until has passed, and a reboot under another declaration neither recomputes nor shortens it. Durable only on the file-backed kernel store with a key ring: restart is witnessed in process and for the separated MAS process started directly (demo/src/mas-pilot/mas-serve.ts through startMasProcess); a relaunch through the launcher (launchMasPilot) is not witnessed. The in-memory default does not survive a restart. Events read back oldest first, so a mapping change is attributable through each event's mapping_version. An operator reads a Mission's events through the operator console's MAS half (GET /missions/{id}/join-evidence, behind its bearer); the MAS serves them on no route of its own. The reference MAS validates no Instance Context as a Context Consumer, so that member is never recorded.

requirements.text: Verify the acting agent (`actor_token`, or the request's client authentication) is authorized to request expansion of this predecessor.

observation.normative: a client not authorized for the predecessor is refused before the creation_request_id lookup, even when it holds the predecessor's token and its key: no deferral or reservation is opened, and no successor is created or predecessor superseded
observation.local: the reference AS authorizes only the predecessor's own client_id (an actor_token is carried, never used to authorize another client, #433) and answers invalid_request with no Mission state. Deferrals persist and the deferred poll runs no initiation check, so the poll also refuses a deferral whose recorded client is not the predecessor's client, answered as an unknown code (invalid_grant) before the key check and before redeem (#1357), decided from the recorded predecessor and not the subject_token; the predecessor's own poll still completes without one (#1326). A successor that another client's poll created before that check existed carries the predecessor's client, and its committed deferral is retained, so building the AS revokes each one the deferral consistently identifies (exactly one Mission carrying the deferral's predecessor and approval event, named by the predecessor's supersession, carrying its client, and no own-client deferral claiming that event), a suspended, committed but unreleased, or late-denied one included (the deferral's completion marker, not its state, selects it). The predecessor stays superseded, a completed or expired successor keeps its termination, a revoked successor's child cascades, a successor its own client approved is untouched, a later boot commits nothing, and the family-grant revocation of a successor the expiry clock terminated is attempted before the AS is returned even when nothing is revoked. The revoked successor's Token Exchange and refresh family are refused and its derivation gate throws, while an access token already issued for it still verifies offline until exp. A committed deferral from another client whose linkage is incomplete or contradicted is reported on the build result, not acted on (#1349): its predecessor or successor names another issuer than this kernel's, its predecessor is missing, it records no approval event, no successor carries that event, the predecessor's supersession names another Mission, the successor lacks the predecessor's client, or an own-client deferral claims the same event; each is reported before the expiry clock runs, neither revoked nor expired (#1392). A Progressive ceiling-drawdown successor opens no deferral, but its basis records the requesting client as activation_actor while its client_id is the predecessor's, so building the AS also revokes each non-terminal drawdown successor whose activation actor names an issuer and a client, whose actor, successor and predecessor all name this kernel's issuer, whose actor names a client other than its own, which carries its predecessor's client, and which the predecessor's supersession names, a suspended one included; own-client, terminal and later own-client successors are left alone and a repeated boot commits nothing. A drawdown whose actor names no client, whose actor or successor names another issuer (including two foreign issuers that agree), whose predecessor is another issuer's or missing, which lacks its predecessor's client, or which the predecessor's supersession does not name is reported before the expiry clock runs, neither revoked nor expired (#1372). Partial: the actor_token arm, authorizing a delegated acting agent through actor_token, is not implemented, so it is not exercised.

requirements.text: the AS creates the Mission Record in the `active` state atomically with the approval decision, and that commit makes the session's `device_code` redeemable

observation.normative: No Mission exists, and polling yields authorization_pending or slow_down, until the decision commits; the Mission exists from that commit, and the device_code becomes redeemable subject to its lifetime, one-time use, and issuance gating.
observation.local: The decision request saves the Mission grant under an identity derived from the interaction, commits the record already bound to it in the kernel store (#916's order of writes), then writes the device code's activation to the provider adapter, all under the session's claim, which every exit releases. A grant-store failure precedes the commit and leaves no Mission; a live failure after the commit (the activation write) leaves an active, bound Mission. Either way the session stays pending, and a retry of the same decision finds the record its approval event created, if any, and rebinds the same derived grant, so it never duplicates the Mission or its grant; a retried record no longer active ends the session denied. A failed decision never retried leaves the Mission to the unredeemed-session rule. Not atomic across a crash: the two stores share no transaction, so a crash between the commit and the activation write leaves an active Mission whose code expires unredeemed (the cross-step domain #250 tracks).

Live failures are witnessed with an injected grant-store fault (before the commit: no Mission) and an injected activation-write fault (after it). Proved by dropping the activation write, by not releasing the claim on a failure, by not reusing the committed grant binding, by giving each retry a new approval event, and by activating a retried Mission that is no longer active. Merged onto #916's order of writes: the retried-but-revoked case now injects its fault at the activation write, and disabling the active check on a retried Mission was re-run and caught; the other proofs ran on the earlier order.

requirements.notes: #816, D830. Proposed from slice 2 (impl/816-budget-reservations 22c1fae0); the capability stays disabled and unclaimed. An unmetered budget binding (currency, undeclared budget, owner, limit, unlisted policy), a remote or ephemeral PDP, an unclaimed declaration, and an unmetered amount-bearing spend are each an evaluated denial (decision false) carrying constraint_unsupported, with no reservation or claim (E1, E2, E3a, E3, E3c, E7, E8, E4, E5, E6, E9, N2 to N5, H1, P4a, P4b). Slice 3b (impl/813-budget-binding-3b at 62325958): a binding the decision point's source answers underivable, throws on, or returns malformed is an evaluated denial (decision false) carrying constraint_unsupported, with no reservation or claim, a read included; through the composed stack such an instance's payment is refused constraint_unsupported. F1, F2, F3 and Z2 fail the decision-point witness; F1, F3, F4, F5 and F5b fail the end-to-end one. The unclaimed and shipped-statement witnesses show the duty also holds without the capability. Merged with #956: an unclassified request is refused before evaluation as action_class_missing, earlier than decision h, so its unclassified case is no longer cited here (the separate pre-evaluation witness shows nothing reserved or claimed). Slice 4 (#816, D877; impl/816-pdp-slice4 at 793d2e85, mutation on impl/816-pdp-track at eeb034e5, the same commits): a constraint_unsupported denial records decision deny and denial_reason constraint_unsupported in its signed, verified Decision Evidence; recording another reason (W17) fails it. #1772 (D907, fix/1772-constraint-unsupported at 8dcec123): a Mission entry carrying a constraints key outside the set the PDP evaluates provides no authority and, with no other applicable entry, is an evaluated denial carrying constraint_unsupported with no authority_bound, never parameter_violation (kept for an evaluated violation), and the Decision Evidence witness reads denial_reason constraint_unsupported for an unrecognized key and for an unmeterable budget; mutants a (the key back to parameter_violation), b (an unsupported entry denies the whole request), c (the key treated as satisfied), d (an evaluated violation reclassified), e and i (the signed reason rewritten for each case), f (the unmetered gate rewritten) and j (refused before evaluation) each fail a cited witness. Credential-specific qualification: a credential entry carrying an unrecognized constraint is denied credential_invalid under authzen#context-credential (the table's credential-authority row), not constraint_unsupported. D929 (fix/1772-constraint-unsupported at 65d6fcf7): the row is unconditional, since refusing an unsupported constraint does not depend on metering.exact-budget and every unrecognized-key witness runs without it; the stage-precedence witnesses (an unsupported entry beside a violated one in either order is parameter_violation, one entry carrying both is constraint_unsupported, a violated credential entry beside an unsupported Mission entry is the credential's parameter_violation) fail under mutants k (constraint_unsupported preferred whenever an entry was unsupported), l (the reason taken from the last entry in array order), m (the unrecognized-key stage run before the credential bound) and n (the unrecognized-key stage run after the constraint stage).

requirements.notes: #1724 D5 (D847). Proved by five defects: the resolver's expected issuer taken from the response (only the throughout-impostor witness fails; the existing iss-only test is caught by check 4 regardless); metadata naming another issuer accepted; keys from a fixed path at the issuer instead of the metadata's jwks_uri; the Status endpoint guessed from where the metadata was read. The launcher's own issuer check (mas-pilot-launcher.test.ts) is not cited: without it the helper still refuses, so its test fails only on the message.
